title: Beyond Deterministic Alignment: Probabilistic Vision–Language Representations for Pedestrian Re-Identification
affiliations: The University of Tokyo, University of Tokyo - Graduate School of Engineering, University of Tokyo - Graduate School of Engineering and University of Tokyo - Graduate School of Engineering

detail.title: Beyond Deterministic Alignment: Probabilistic Vision–Language Representations for Pedestrian Re-Identification
detail.abstract: Uncertainty estimation plays an important role in perception tasks for autonomous systems. Motivated by CLIP-based uncertainty modal modeling, this study formulates pedestrian representations as probabilistic embeddings rather than fixed feature vectors. A variational learning strategy is employed to model both data-dependent and model-related uncertainty across visual and textual modalities. The approach is evaluated on three pedestrian re-identification benchmarks containing over 95,000 identities and 780,000 images. Performance is compared with deterministic baselines, including ResNet-based ReID, Transformer-based ReID, and CLIP-derived embedding models. Results show average gains of 3.1% in rank-1 accuracy and 3.7% in mAP, along with a reduction of expected calibration error by 18%-24% in occlusion-heavy scenarios.

title: Learning Occlusion-Robust Pedestrian Representations via Uncertainty-Guided Feature Pruning
affiliations: Technical University of Munich, Technische Universität München (TUM) - Department of Informatics and Technische Universität München (TUM) - Department of Informatics

detail.title: Learning Occlusion-Robust Pedestrian Representations via Uncertainty-Guided Feature Pruning
detail.abstract: Occlusion and background interference remain major challenges for pedestrian re-identification in urban traffic environments. Inspired by uncertainty-aware CLIP-based frameworks, this paper introduces an uncertainty-guided feature selection mechanism that adjusts the contribution of local visual regions and semantic cues according to their estimated reliability. The proposed method is evaluated on two autonomous driving datasets with both real-world and synthetic occlusion patterns, covering occlusion ratios from 20% to 60%. Comparisons are conducted against attention-based and part-based ReID methods, including PCB, OSNet, and transformer-based attention models. The proposed approach achieves mAP improvements ranging from 4.5% to 6.2% under severe occlusion conditions, while maintaining comparable performance in fully visible settings.

title: Adapting Vision Language Pedestrian Re Identification across Cities via Uncertainty Reweighting
affiliations: University of Toronto, University of Toronto - Department of Computer Science and University of Toronto - Department of Computer Science

detail.title: Adapting Vision Language Pedestrian Re Identification across Cities via Uncertainty Reweighting
detail.abstract: Autonomous driving deployments face open-set conditions where many pedestrians do not belong to any known identity gallery. Motivated by uncertainty-aware CLIP-based modal modeling, this paper introduces an uncertainty-calibrated similarity scoring scheme that supports both identification and unknown rejection. The framework estimates uncertainty from vision-language embedding disagreement and uses temperature-scaled calibration to improve decision reliability. Evaluations are performed on open-set protocols with 180,000 query images and mixed galleries where 30%-60% of queries correspond to unseen identities. Compared with softmax-threshold and distance-based open-set baselines using TransReID and CLIP embeddings, the proposed approach increases AUROC for unknown detection by 6.5%-9.2% while maintaining closed-set mAP within a 1.0% margin. At a fixed false accept rate, false matches drop by 20%-27% in heavy occlusion subsets.

title: The Universal Benefit Ethic (UBE): An Artificial Intelligence Ethical Principle That We Can All Support
affiliations: InfoSecurity Infrastructure, Inc.

detail.title: The Universal Benefit Ethic (UBE): An Artificial Intelligence Ethical Principle That We Can All Support

detail.abstract: The lack of a consensus about the relevant ethics for AI systems has not materially interfered with the many deployments throughout our modern world. This lack of consensus permits the development and public release of dangerous AI systems, systems that may never have been built or publicly released if they had been governed by the ethical principle described herein. With new developments in the AI realm coming at an incredibly rapid and exponentially increasing pace, it is urgent that we establish a better foundation of sanity, reality, truth, and generally-agreed-upon ethics on which all high-risk AI systems must be built and operated. To that end, this paper describes a new, long overdue, and pervasively applicable ethical principle that helps to build-in the safety, rationality, and grounded perspective that we so urgently need in the age of AI-related hype and hyperbole. More specifically, the paper defines the Universal Benefit Ethic (UBE), a judgment by a third-party committee of independent assessors, who vote and collectively determine whether, on a net basis, the high-risk AI system in question is beneficial to all stakeholder groups who will be materially affected by the system. This UBE approach has many benefits including: (1) assist with alignment between human values and AI system values, (2) help reduce uncertainty regarding the future impacts of AI, especially after Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) comes onto the scene, (3) establish a mechanism to counterbalance our dysfunctional economical-and-power-oriented decision-making system, (4) check and prevent the concentration of AI-augmented power in the hands of a few, (5) limit the use of powerful AI systems by bad actors such as organized crime syndicates, unscrupulous businesses, and dictatorial governments, (6) create a universal guiding principle for future AI system evolution, and (7) agree to a readily-accepted reason to shutdown rogue and/or destructive AI systems.

title: Objective Plasticity and Phase Transitions in Long-Horizon Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: Clevix AI Research and Clevix LLC

detail.title: Objective Plasticity and Phase Transitions in Long-Horizon Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: Reinforcement learning systems often achieve strong performance on short-horizon tasks, yet struggle to make sustained progress when learning must unfold over long horizons. We identify the root cause not in optimization failures, but in structural rigidity of learning objectives themselves. This work introduces Objective Plasticity & Phase Transition (OPPT), a theoretical framework that treats the learning objective itself as a dynamical state governing reward functions, conservatism thresholds, admissibility constraints, and planning horizons. We establish two complementary results. First, we prove a necessity theorem showing that when the objective evolves rigidly, the volume (Lebesgue measure) of reachable behavioral trajectories contracts monotonically, yielding unavoidable long-horizon performance ceilings regardless of optimization quality. Second, we show that when the objective exhibits sufficient plasticity, learning progress occurs through a developmental phase transition marked by a discontinuous expansion of reachable trajectories. This transition enables access to previously unreachable behavioral regimes and produces a qualitative jump in long-horizon capability. Taken together, these results suggest that long-horizon stagnation is rooted in structural properties of fixed objectives, and that sustained progress requires changing how objectives evolve rather than optimizing harder. Scope Note: This work focuses on theoretical properties of reinforcement learning systems and does not address consciousness, general intelligence, or non-algorithmic notions of agency.

title: The Indian Media Revolution: A Multigenerational Analysis of Technology, Social Change, and the Ascendancy of Short-Form Video
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Indian Media Revolution: A Multigenerational Analysis of Technology, Social Change, and the Ascendancy of Short-Form Video
detail.abstract: This report presents a comprehensive examination of the transformation of India’s media ecosystem, tracing its trajectory from state-controlled broadcasting to today’s fragmented and digital-first environment. It begins with the foundational roles of All India Radio (AIR) and Doordarshan, whose growth reflected centralized regulation until liberalization opened the market to competition. The study highlights the democratization of the internet, with Reliance Jio’s disruptive entry making data affordable and catalyzing widespread adoption of digital platforms. This milestone fueled the exponential rise of social media, marked by the decline of early platforms like Orkut, the consolidation of global players, and the emergence of Indian alternatives. The analysis further investigates generational usage patterns, contrasting youth-driven trends with older demographics who use social media for connectivity. The report emphasizes the dual nature of these platforms, recognizing their capacity to mobilize social movements while underscoring challenges such as misinformation and the documented links to mental health issues. The concluding section focuses on the “Reels Revolution,” presenting evidence that short-form video content has overtaken television in viewership. Expert perspectives are incorporated to underscore the neurological and psychological implications of this shift, particularly regarding attention, focus, and cognitive well-being.

title: GenAI-Enabled Causal Study of Unstructured Data
affiliations: University of Texas at Austin - Department of Information, Risk and Operations Management, University of Texas at Austin and The University of Texas at Austin

detail.title: GenAI-Enabled Causal Study of Unstructured Data
detail.abstract: Information systems (IS) researchers often use machine learning algorithms to extract features in massive and unstructured online content and then study the causal effect of these features on various business outcomes. Generative AI (GenAI), as automatic unstructured data analyzers, offer new opportunities for IS researchers to advance the current causal study of unstructured data. Nevertheless, we show that directly plugging GenAI-generated variables into econometric models can induce bias in causal estimation. We propose a novel algorithm to correct such bias. A key feature is that the algorithm leverages predictions generated by different GenAIs to form fuzzy interval data. The algorithm meets three design requirements. First, it is unsupervised, meaning it does not need additional labeled data to correct the causal estimation. Second, it is flexible in incorporating the predictions of different GenAIs (leveraging the "wisdom of the AI crowd") and can be easily adapted to various causal models. Third, the causal estimators are theoretically guaranteed to achieve consistency. We apply our algorithm in the context of using LLMs as emotion analyzers. This work provides important implications for causal inference with GenAIs, the causal study of unstructured data, and prescriptive analytics for fuzzy interval data.

title: KEVP: The Kessari Edge Validation Protocol for High-Throughput zk Rollups: A Formal Systems Architecture for Verifiable Edge-Cached Blockchain Transactions
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: KEVP: The Kessari Edge Validation Protocol for High-Throughput zk Rollups: A Formal Systems Architecture for Verifiable Edge-Cached Blockchain Transactions
detail.abstract: This paper presents the Kessari Edge Validation Protocol (KEVP), a formal systems architecture for achieving low-latency, high-throughput blockchain transactions through the integration of zkvalidity rollups, verifiable edge caching, and software-defined networking principles. I introduce a three-layer model consisting of (1) a minimal Layer-1 settlement chain providing deterministic finality, (2) a custom Layer-2 zk execution environment based on application-specific primitives, and (3) an officially hosted edge network that delivers cryptographically verifiable preconfirmations and proof-backed state reads. Unlike traditional blockchain RPC models, KEVP formalizes the role of edge infrastructure within the verification stack. All user-facing responses are independently verifiable using Merkle proofs anchored to Layer-1-accepted zk proofs, ensuring that performance optimizations do not introduce additional trust assumptions. The protocol enables parallel execution through structured access lists, amortizes proving costs via batched zk circuits, and applies SDN-based routing to optimize latency-sensitive traffic. I formally define the KEVP protocol workflow, caching semantics, threat model, and verification procedures, and present a concrete instantiation using five custom zk primitives designed for integrity-economy workloads. Analytical performance modeling suggests that KEVP is capable of supporting Visa-level user experience while preserving full cryptographic correctness and decentralized settlement. Empirical validation of these performance characteristics is reserved for future work. This paper is intentionally focused on systems architecture, protocol design, and security analysis. Broader economic, application-specific, and ecosystem implications are addressed in companion work on the Kessari and IntelliFi platforms.

title: Pricing, Technology, and Enforcement in Markets with Digital Piracy: A Hotelling Approach
affiliations: Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research and Jawaharlal Nehru University

detail.title: Pricing, Technology, and Enforcement in Markets with Digital Piracy: A Hotelling Approach
detail.abstract: We analyze the strategic interaction between an original content provider and a pirate firm in a spatial Hotelling framework. The model accounts for technological difficulty and probabilistic enforcement as determinants of consumer adoption and firm profits. Under uniform distributions, we derive closed-form equilibrium prices, technological effort, and market shares. Comparative statics reveal how enforcement intensity, technological barriers, and pirate revenue parameters shape equilibrium outcomes. While the original and pirate firms are pure substitutes in market share, their pricing and technological strategies display strategic complementarities. The results clarify how regulatory interventions and technological investments influence market power and profitability. By combining analytical tractability with flexible specifications for pirate costs and revenues, the framework provides clear insights for policymakers and managers addressing digital piracy.

detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence systems scale in capability, persistent user memory, identity, and reasoning are increasingly consolidated within centralized model providers. This concentration creates governance, security, and power-alignment risks that policy mechanisms alone cannot fully mitigate. This paper proposes Artificially Distributed System Intelligence (ADSI), a layered architecture that separates execution, identity, governance, and capability into distinct components with explicit trust boundaries. ADSI embeds authority constraints directly into system structure through a Sovereign Control Plane and bounded intent mediation, enabling scalable intelligence delegation without centralized ownership of persistent user context. The paper formalizes the system model, adversary assumptions, and bounded guarantees of the architecture.

title: Institutional Context and Nurse Manager Preparedness for Mentorship Roles in a Tertiary Hospital in Kenya
affiliations: Kenya Methodist University (KeMU)

detail.title: Institutional Context and Nurse Manager Preparedness for Mentorship Roles in a Tertiary Hospital in Kenya
detail.abstract:
Background: Mentorship plays a crucial role in the professional development of nurses, emphasizing a patient-centric approach to nursing care. However, there exists a lack of clarity regarding the preparatory measures for nurses in charge, posing challenges in effectively conveying their multifaceted roles. Globally, (Manion et al., 2021) argues that preparedness of nurse managers in mentorship roles is pivotal. According to (WHO, 2020), in Sub-Saharan Africa, nurse managers are tasked with an intricate interplay of leadership, management, and mentorship roles, demanding a nuanced understanding of these roles. Nurse managers need effective mentorship training to improve their effectiveness in their roles (KNH, 2019).

Objectives: This study aimed to assess institutional factors associated with the preparedness of nurse managers for mentorship roles: a case of Kenyatta National Hospital. The focus was on leadership, policy, motivation, and training factors.

Methods: The study employed a descriptive cross-sectional design, utilizing a simple random sampling strategy to engage 88 respondents. Data collection involved a carefully designed semi-structured self-administered questionnaire comprising a blend of open-ended and closed-ended inquiries to ensure a comprehensive exploration. Prior to this study, a pre-test was done at KUTRRH to improve the tool's validity and reliability. The resultant quantitative data was analyzed using SPSS version 27. Data was presented through tables, figures, and pie charts. Necessary permissions were obtained from relevant
authorities. Participants were informed about study objectives before consenting. Numerical codes were used to ensure privacy on questionnaires, meticulously secured when not in use. Correlation coefficient was used to determine the association between variables.

Results: Key findings revealed that most nurse managers at Kenyatta National Hospital are female, with an average age above 50 years, and possess 2 to 5 years of working experience, with the majority holding a bachelor's degree in nursing. While 42% of participants were moderately prepared for mentorship roles, 58% were inadequately prepared due to time constraints, workload, and lack of management support. There was a positive correlation between workload and preparedness for mentorship (r = .411, p<.01) and between involvement in policy-making and preparedness (r = .281, p=.008). Additionally, there was a significant association between the provision of standards on mentorship (r = 3.18, p=.02) and training programs (r = 3.18, p=.02) with preparedness. Many participants (58%) felt motivated due to remunerations and allowances, though only 38% attended training programs specifically for mentorship. Nurses were not actively involved in policy-making processes, leading to a lack of clear guidelines for mentorship programs despite existing standard operating procedures within nurse manager units. Although nurse managers were incentivized by remuneration and training incentives, the absence of feedback on their performance as mentors proved demotivating. Lack of communication with senior management hinders their preparedness for mentorship roles.

Conclusion: Nurse managers preparedness in mentorship roles could be significantly enhanced through
support. The study recommends increased leadership support, clearer guidelines on mentorship roles,
involvement in policy-making, and provision of resources such as time and reduced workload to enhance
nurse manager preparedness for mentorship roles.

title: Econometric Analysis of Diminishing Marginal Returns in Closed Platform Ecosystems: Empirical Evidence of the "Liquidity Trap" in Amazon FBA

detail.title: Econometric Analysis of Diminishing Marginal Returns in Closed Platform Ecosystems: Empirical Evidence of the "Liquidity Trap" in Amazon FBA
detail.abstract: This study examines the financial viability of the Amazon FBA (Fulfillment by Amazon) model for Third-Party Sellers through a multivariable regression analysis applied to a real transactional dataset. The results reject the null hypothesis that a higher Gross Merchandise Volume ($GMV$) leads proportionally to higher net profitability ($\pi$). Conversely, the econometric evidence suggests a negative correlation ($r = -0.14$) between inventory growth and Free Cash Flow, demonstrating that the platform's fee structure (Fees, PPC, Storage) acts as a progressive tax that erodes EBITDA margin, driving SMEs into a zone of technical insolvency despite growth in gross revenue.

title: Towards a Strategic Research Agenda on Startup Labor Markets
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - Management Department, IESE Business School and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Towards a Strategic Research Agenda on Startup Labor Markets
detail.abstract: The entrepreneurship literature has traditionally emphasized the human capital of founders and founding teams. Yet as startups move from founding to scaling, their performance increasingly depends on how they engage with labor markets beyond the founding and top management teams. We argue that startup labor markets constitute a distinct and underexplored strategic domain in entrepreneurship research, one that governs how ventures attract, structure, develop, and retain talent under conditions of uncertainty. We organize this agenda around three structural features that distinguish startups from more established firms and generate distinctive labor market frictions: (1) uncertainty about product-market fit, which creates ambiguous roles and learning environments; (2) resource and reputational scarcity, which complicates pricing and signaling to prospective employees; and (3) high failure risk, which elevates career risk and shapes mobility expectations. For each feature, we examine implications for both startups (the demand side) and workers (the supply side), highlighting the strategic tradeoffs embedded in hiring, compensation, job design, and mobility. We identify priority directions for future research across entry and sorting, work and incentives, development and learning, and mobility and market shaping, and we discuss data sources that enable empirical progress. Overall, we aim to reorient strategic entrepreneurship research from a primary focus on entrepreneurial founding toward a labor-mediated view of enterprise scaling, in which talent and labor market strategy are central to competitive advantage.

title: Sherlocking: The Effects of Platform-Owner Entry on the Competitive Behavior of Third-Party Firms

detail.title: Sherlocking: The Effects of Platform-Owner Entry on the Competitive Behavior of Third-Party Firms

publicationDetails.detailsText: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: I study how third-party firms respond when a platform owner enters its own marketplace, analyzing Apple's entries into App Store submarkets from 2016-2021. Using text embeddings to define markets and a staggered difference-indifferences design, I find that Apple's entry deters new competitors and shifts incumbents' monetization strategies, but effects vary widely: many markets show no meaningful response, while others move in opposing directions across a host of monetization and quality outcomes. Responses depend on how Apple enters and apps' competitive proximity to Apple. This heterogeneity suggests targeted oversight rather than categorical restrictions on platform-owner entry.

title: Strategic Management Psychology (SMP) A Diagnostic Framework for Strategic Blindness and Decision Incompetence
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Strategic Management Psychology (SMP) A Diagnostic Framework for Strategic Blindness and Decision Incompetence
detail.abstract: Despite significant advances in strategic management, behavioral strategy, and organizational decisionmaking, organizations repeatedly fail to recognize, frame, and respond effectively to major strategic disruptions. This persistent pattern suggests that strategic failure is not primarily a problem of information, resources, or execution, but rather a failure of strategic diagnosis. This paper introduces Strategic Management Psychology (SMP) as a distinct conceptual and diagnostic field focused on the psychological substrates of strategic blindness, diagnostic incompetence, and organizational inertia. SMP examines how senior decision-makers perceive, interpret, and classify strategic phenomena, and how these cognitive and psychological processes systematically shape strategic responses. Using the contemporary case of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as an illustrative context, the paper demonstrates how misdiagnosis at the cognitive and governance levels leads to predictable and recurring strategic errors. The study positions SMP as complementary to, yet conceptually distinct from, behavioral strategy and organizational psychology, offering a structured diagnostic lens for analyzing strategic decision-making failures in complex and uncertain environments.

title: Feedback trading, risk aversion, and their relationship: New evidence from the crude oil markets
affiliations: University of Waikato - Management School, University of Waikato - Management School, University of Waikato - Department of Economics and Finance, University of Birmingham and University of Waikato

detail.title: Feedback trading, risk aversion, and their relationship: New evidence from the crude oil markets
detail.abstract: The irrational feedback trading behavior in the crude oil markets remains puzzling for academic communities and market professionals. This study explores the time-varying features of feedback trading in the four major crude oil futures markets. We find the popularity of positive feedback trading in the WTI, Brent and DME Oman futures markets, and that of negative feedback trading in the China SIEE futures market. However, substantial oscillations of feedback trading strategies occur over time, where positive and negative feedback trading strategies cluster during miscella- neous market crises. Further, risk aversion plays a dominant role in the dynamic mean and volatility transmissions with feedback trading in most of the crude oil markets. The dominance of risk aver- sion is more pronounced during the tumultuous periods such as GFC and COVID-19 pandemic. Our findings render important implications for investors on containing irrational feedback trading.

title: Beyond Stereotypes: Understanding Masculinity in the Male
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Beyond Stereotypes: Understanding Masculinity in the Male
detail.abstract: This study, Beyond Stereotypes: Understanding Masculinity in the Male, explores the multidimensional nature of masculinity through psychological, sociocultural, evolutionary, and anthropological perspectives. It critically examines the concept of the “young male syndrome,” emphasizing heightened risk-taking behavior, aggression, competitiveness, and status-seeking tendencies among adolescent and young adult males. The work integrates cross-cultural case studies, historical narratives, and scientific research to demonstrate that masculinity is neither static nor universally defined but shaped through complex interactions between biology, culture, and social expectations. It highlights evolutionary theories related to reproductive competition, testosterone influence, and sexual dimorphism, alongside sociological frameworks such as dominance and prestige-based status acquisition. The study also evaluates how modern societal transformations, including digital environments, changing labor structures, and shifting gender roles, influence male identity formation. By incorporating personal narrative elements and comparative global data, the research emphasizes the importance of structured mentorship, cultural guidance, and institutional responsibility in channeling male ambition toward constructive social contributions. Ultimately, the work seeks to move beyond stereotypical portrayals of masculinity by presenting a balanced and evidence-based interpretation of male psychological development and social behavior.

title: CBDCs vs. Cryptocurrencies: Comparative Analysis of Privacy Approaches Using NLP

detail.title: CBDCs vs. Cryptocurrencies: Comparative Analysis of Privacy Approaches Using NLP
detail.abstract: Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) and cryptocurrencies differ significantly in terms of privacy and regulatory compliance. While cryptocurrencies provide strong anonymity, CBDCs cannot follow the same design. As state-issued digital currencies, they must embed regulatory compliance directly into their architecture while potentially incorporating Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs) to protect user data. This paper provides an overview of how different PETs are used in CBDCs and cryptocurrencies. Using Natural Language Processing (NLP) on a corpus of 177 documents covering four major CBDCs (DCash, eNaira, JAM-DEX, Sand Dollar) and four cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Monero, Zcash), we analyse how privacy concepts and PETs are framed. Findings reveal that cryptocurrencies embed privacy at a technical level, while CBDCs treat PETs mainly as conceptual compliance tools, highlighting distinct paradigms in privacy implementation.

title: The impact of disability-targeted job training programme on labour market outcomes: Results from a cluster-randomised control trial in Bangladesh
affiliations: London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, BRAC University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, BRAC University and London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine - International Centre for Evidence in Disability

detail.title: The impact of disability-targeted job training programme on labour market outcomes: Results from a cluster-randomised control trial in Bangladesh
detail.abstract: In Bangladesh, youth with disabilities are four times more likely to be out of school and work than youth without disabilities. Yet there is a lack of evidence both in Bangladesh and globally on how to improve employment outcomes for this group. This paper presents results from a cluster-randomised control trial of a job training program targeted to youth with disabilities. The trial was conducted between January 2022-March 2024 across 39 of the 64 districts of Bangladesh and involved 1,481 youth with disabilities. The STAR+ programme is run by BRAC, one of the largest development organizations in the world, and targets youth with disabilities (ages 14-35) who are out of school and work, and from households living in poverty. It combines classroom and on-the-job training (apprenticeship) for youth with disabilities, alongside other components (e.g., workplace accessibility audits, sensitisation of employers and communities). In the intention-to-treat analysis, the STAR+ programme increased the likelihoods of being employed by 22% (4.2 percentage points - pp), and both hours worked and earnings by 33% at 16 months post-completion of the interventions. Heterogeneity analysis found that the program was equally effective for men and women, and for people with different severities of functional limitations. It had a large effect for youth with disabilities with some formal education (8.2 pp increase in employment and 42% increase in earnings), but no statistically significant effect for youth without any formal education (-3.6 pp) and a negative impact for youth with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

title: Exploring Gold Price Dynamics through Bibliometric Mapping and PRISMA based Systematic Review
affiliations: Sambalpur University, Sambalpur University - Department of Business Administration and Sambalpur University

detail.title: Exploring Gold Price Dynamics through Bibliometric Mapping and PRISMA based Systematic Review
detail.abstract: Gold has long served as a cornerstone of financial stability, yet its role in modern portfolios is increasingly contested by digital assets and shaped by macroeconomic volatility. This study offers a unique synthesis that combines bibliometric mapping with systematic review techniques of gold price research (2020–2025), capturing the field’s evolution through crises like the COVID-19 pandemic and the rise of cryptocurrencies. Analyzing 1,366 records from Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Dimensions, we distill insights from 155 peer-reviewed articles using VOSviewer for bibliometric mapping and PRISMA 2020 guidelines for thematic synthesis, and the MMAT 2018 tool for methodological quality assessment.Three key findings emerge. First, inflation, interest rates, and USD exchange rates remain gold’s primary macroeconomic anchors, though their impacts vary across economic regimes. Second, gold’s safe-haven status persists but faces competition from Bitcoin during short-term shocks, revealing a nuanced hedging landscape. Third, forecasting methodologies have shifted decisively, machine learning techniques such as LSTM and XGBoost surpass traditional econometric models like ARIMA and GARCH in forecasting accuracy, though their limited transparency continues to pose interpretability challenges—prompting innovation through hybrid and explainable frameworks.The study reveals a fragmented yet growing research ecosystem, dominated by China, India, and the U.S., with limited cross-border collaboration. Practical implications extend to investors navigating multi-asset portfolios and policymakers calibrating gold-backed strategies in inflation-prone economies. We call for future work to integrate ESG factors, high-frequency data, and Global South perspectives, ensuring gold research reflects contemporary financial complexities.

title: Forward Guidance in the Nonlinear New Keynesian Model

detail.title: Forward Guidance in the Nonlinear New Keynesian Model
detail.abstract: The forward-guidance puzzle refers to the implausibly large effects of anticipated future interest rate changes on current output and inflation, as predicted by standard New Keynesian models. In this paper, we analyze both theoretically and numerically the nonlinear model that underlies the canonical linearized framework, explicitly tracking the full distribution of prices across firms. We show that large output expansions arise only under extreme and economically implausible circumstances: firms that are unable to reset prices are forced to sell below marginal cost while satisfying unbounded demand, thereby accumulating arbitrarily large losses. When we modify the model so that non-reoptimizing firms can at least set prices equal to marginal cost, output and inflation remain bounded and moderate. However, under this modification not all forward-guidance announcements are feasible in equilibrium. Our results identify a neglected microeconomic assumption as the root cause of the forward-guidance puzzle and clarify the limits of New Keynesian models in the analysis of large or persistent monetary shocks.

detail.abstract: This paper provides scholarly context, comparative analysis, and novelty positioning for the AI Non-Delegation Doctrine v1.2.2. The doctrine establishes a sector-agnostic constraint: optimisation may be delegated; responsibility may not. It formalises non-delegation as a structural governance boundary applicable wherever AI systems materially influence high-consequence decisions. This paper does not interpret, extend, or modify the doctrine. It situates the doctrine within existing legal, policy, military, ethical, and socio-technical literature concerning delegation, accountability, and human authority in automated decision systems. It identifies areas of conceptual convergenceparticularly with constitutional non-delegation theory, human-in-command models, and agency laundering critiques-while clarifying the doctrine's distinct contributions. The doctrine's originality lies not in identifying novel concerns, but in formalising them as a closed, prospective, and enforceable governance instrument. It introduces a prospective violation test, formalises refusal as a mandatory outcome under certain conditions, and separates authority from evidence or consensus claims. This companion paper is external and non-authoritative. In the event of inconsistency, the doctrine prevails.

title: Investigating Overconfidence Bias in the Bangladesh Equity Market: New Evidence from a Deep Learning Approach Across Distinct Market States
affiliations: United International University and University of Dhaka

detail.title: Investigating Overconfidence Bias in the Bangladesh Equity Market: New Evidence from a Deep Learning Approach Across Distinct Market States
detail.abstract: The paper examines overconfidence bias employing a deep learning Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) approach. This framework comprehensively captures non-linear and temporal dependencies between trading activity and equity market returns across diverse market states: bearish, bullish, crisis, extended crisis, and COVID-19. Applying an advanced machine learning model in overconfidence study offers a methodological advancement beyond the constraints of traditional econometric models. The study introduces a distinctive behavioral perspective by segregating market returns into expected and unexpected components, where the latter extracted from the market Index Model, reflects investors’ reactions to surprising market movements. The findings confirm that LSTM focusing on total returns exhibits overconfident behavior in the overall, bearish, and crisis phases; however, incorporating unexpected return further extends its presence to the extended crisis market. This behavioral pattern characterizes a defensive manifestation of overconfidence in which investors continue to trade excessively in crisis driven environments, particularly during market downturn. The combination of machine learning with market state-based framework strengthens behavioral finance research and yields significant insights for researchers, policymakers, and market participants in frontier market settings.

title: Regulation and Governance in Oil and Gas Investment: Comparative Insights from Norway, Canada, And Venezuela

detail.title: Regulation and Governance in Oil and Gas Investment: Comparative Insights from Norway, Canada, And Venezuela
detail.abstract: This paper examines how regulatory governance influences oil and gas investment outcomes through a comparative analysis of Norway, Canada, and Venezuela. Using a comparative law approach, it evaluates each jurisdiction’s petroleum regulatory framework, historical development, market performance, political conditions, and legal protections for foreign investors, with particular attention to U.S. investment considerations.

detail.abstract: This nomination examines the strategic role of the Government of Indonesia in managing the conflict surrounding the Air Weapon Range (AWR) Siabu in Kampar Regency, Riau Province, as a contribution to sustainable peace, national security, and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The AWR Siabu conflict represents a complex interaction between military defense imperatives, environmental security, and the socioeconomic rights of local communities. Drawing upon expert perspectives in security studies, conflict transformation, environmental governance, and sustainable development, this study adopts an integrated analytical framework combining the Human Security Model, the Whole-of-Government approach, and the Environmental Security paradigm. Using qualitative policy analysis supported by institutional and regulatory review, the study demonstrates that conventional state-centric security approaches are insufficient to address conflicts involving strategic military infrastructure and civilian livelihoods. Instead, the findings highlight that inclusive governance, cross-sectoral coordination, environmental accountability, and participatory conflict transformation are critical for preventing escalation and sustaining peace. The Indonesian government's evolving strategies-such as inter-agency coordination, community dialogue mechanisms, environmental rehabilitation, and adaptive defense policiesillustrate how national security objectives can be reconciled with human security and sustainable development principles. The AWR Siabu case offers a replicable peacebuilding model that transforms defense-related conflict into an opportunity for strengthening social cohesion, institutional legitimacy, and environmental sustainability. As such, this initiative exemplifies a practical contribution to positive peace, aligning national defense governance with SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The nomination underscores that sustainable peace in the contemporary era is achieved not through militarization alone, but through governance models that integrate security, justice, and human dignity.

title: VAT on Private School Fees: Implications for Socioeconomic Mobility in the UK

detail.title: VAT on Private School Fees: Implications for Socioeconomic Mobility in the UK
detail.abstract: This opinion paper explores the proposed introduction of a 20% Value Added Tax (VAT) on private school fees in the UK and its implications for socioeconomic mobility. While the policy is designed as a redistributive means to lessen educational inequality and boost funding for public schools, its ramifications are more complicated. Drawing on extant research on private school education, intergenerational mobility, and the price elasticity of demand, this paper argues that this VAT will perhaps impose a disproportionately greater burden on upper-middleincome households than on the wealthiest. As a result, the policy risks restricting access to private education for upwardly mobile middle-class families, while significantly preserving the structural advantages afforded by elite education. Moreover, increased student mobility from private to public schools could place additional burdens on already under-resourced public schools, potentially undermining the intended equity goals of the policy. By examining tax policy within the broader institutional and social context of educational stratification, this study sheds light on the need to evaluate fiscal interventions not only through the lens of revenue generation but also by considering their unintended effects on social mobility and educational inequality.

title: Why Innovation is Not Enough: Transformative Science and Technology Capability in Developing Economies

detail.title: Why Innovation is Not Enough: Transformative Science and Technology Capability in Developing Economies
detail.abstract: Although many developing economies have invested heavily in science, technology, and innovation, long-term structural transformation and productivity growth have remained slow. The constraint lies not in a lack of innovation itself, but in the absence of a systemic transformative capability at the national level. Building on the theory of National Transformative Capability previously proposed by the author, this study develops the concept of Transformative Science and Technology Capability as a core mechanism through which scientific knowledge and technological potential are translated into substantive economic change. From this perspective, science and technology are not merely inputs to innovation, but a capability to orient development goals, embed technological learning within productive activities, and adapt institutions over time. Transformative science and technology capability is conceptualized as comprising three closely interrelated elements: strategic orientation, productive learning and upgrading, and institutional adaptability. This approach helps explain why many countries exhibit innovation without achieving sustained structural transformation, and it opens new avenues for rethinking development strategies based on science and technology.

detail.abstract: Pedestrians in non-upright postures-those who have fallen due to medical emergencies, intoxication, or primary collisions-represent a significant yet underserved demographic in automotive safety research. Forensic database analyses demonstrate that prostrate road users are disproportionately implicated in hit-and-run incidents. Despite the proliferation of Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS), standard monocular architectures yield a True Positive Rate (TPR) as low as 21.4% for low-profile human targets at night. This paper argues for a paradigm shift: from post-mortem forensic analysis to proactive prevention through the integration of ISO 26262 functional safety standards and multi-modal AI. Drawing on the Advanced Falling Object Detection System (AFODS), we demonstrate that detection accuracy for prone individuals can be raised to 98.2% TPR.

title: AI and Electoral Integrity: Challenges, Cases, and Regulatory Responses in Modern Democracy

detail.title: AI and Electoral Integrity: Challenges, Cases, and Regulatory Responses in Modern Democracy
detail.abstract: AI has significantly affected different aspects of governance while its effects on the values of democracies have raised global concern. This paper concerns how different AI systems, particularly deepfakes, predictive analytics, and misinformation, are utilized to sway voters in democratic processes. With AI's ability to handle large amounts of data and generate convincing but fake content, AI is a strategic asset for political actors seeking to determine voters' choices. A recent example can be considered the 2024 Indian General Election in which artificial intelligence impacts a democratic context. From political ads targeted based on social, economic, and behavioural data to AI-based chatbots for engaging the voters, AI has redrawn the map of political communication. However, at the same time, it was instrumental to people's practical lives, AI was a source of fake news such as the fake videos of Bollywood stars giving their opinions on political leaders. The famous scandal with Cambridge Analytical also presents another significant example to which ethical issues connected with AI and Big data relate. Although it is a British consultancy firm, it stole the personal data of millions of Facebook users unlawfully for political advertising to manipulate important elections including the presidential elections in the United States in 2016 and the Brexit elections. This case makes it clear why the use of personal data for political purposes is an ethical and regulatory concern. During the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election, this research discovered that deepfake AI with political figures as subjects has led to the manipulation of the democratic process. Consequently, this paper proposes the necessity of a broad over-evaluation of the integrity of democracy in the AI context and investigates the demand for the legislation regulation of potential threats of AI manipulation to democracy.

detail.abstract: This chapter examines the evolution of women's roles on the global stage, highlighting their transformative impact across political, social and economic spheres since the late 19th century. It chronicles their journey from historical marginalization to becoming influential decision-makers, peace negotiators and advocates for justice. Key milestones include the waves of feminism, the suffrage movement, the establishment of international women's rights frameworks and the growing presence of women in leadership positions. The chapter also addresses the ongoing challenges in achieving gender parity, particularly in economic empowerment and political participation. Additionally, it explores the various policies, institutions and mechanisms designed specifically to uplift women. Ultimately, it demonstrates how women's participation is redefining leadership and fostering a better society in an interconnected world.

title: Strategic Coordination Capacity and Transformational Thresholds in National Development Trajectories

detail.title: Strategic Coordination Capacity and Transformational Thresholds in National Development Trajectories
detail.abstract: Many developing and middle-income countries have implemented institutional reforms and increased investment in science, technology, and innovation, yet have failed to achieve sustained structural transformation. This article extends the Theory of National Transformative Capability by conceptualizing strategic coordination capacity and placing transformational thresholds at the center of analysis to clarify the non-linear nature of development. It argues that national transformation occurs only when strategic coordination capacity is strong enough to integrate reforms and enable the system to cross critical thresholds. Once these thresholds are crossed, positive development feedback loops are activated, generating a point of no return in which structural upgrading and high-quality growth become endogenous to the system, making a return to low-development trajectories increasingly difficult. The paper contributes a theoretical framework that explains why countries with broadly similar policies experience markedly different long-term development outcomes

New investors and digital platforms have emerged and reshape how creative works and rights are valued and monetized across diverse cultural contexts. title: Reducing Feed Wastage and Stress in Catfish Farming

detail.title: Reducing Feed Wastage and Stress in Catfish Farming
detail.abstract: In catfish farming, feed is both the engine and the expense. It fuels growth, determines harvest size, and quietly decides whether a farm ends the season profitable or struggling. At the same time, feed is where most wastage occurs and where stress, often invisible, begins to take root in fish populations. Pellets sink uneaten, water quality degrades, fish compete aggressively, and farmers respond by adding more feed, hoping to compensate. The cycle repeats, slowly eroding margins and animal welfare at once. What makes this problem particularly complex is that feed wastage and fish stress are not separate issues. They are deeply entangled. Poor feeding practices increase stress, and stressed fish convert feed less efficiently, leading to even more waste². For small and medium scale catfish farmers, especially in regions where aquaculture is both a livelihood and a food security strategy, this feedback loop can be devastating. This article explores how feed wastage and stress emerge in catfish farming, why traditional solutions often fall short, and how integrated, data informed, and biologically sensitive practices can reduce losses while improving fish welfare. The future of sustainable catfish farming will depend not on feeding more, but on feeding smarter.

detail.abstract: Biomass is the most basic energy source especially in poor households and in rural areas, particularly subsistence farmers living in rural areas in developing countries often lack adequate access to basic infrastructure, electricity and modern fuels. This study therefore explores the access and utilization of biomass as fuel energy by rural households in Nkanu West local government of Enugu State. The specific objectives were to examine the Socio-economic characteristics of rural household, identify the various sources and access to biomass by rural households, investigate the constraints to access of biomass, identify different uses and the level of utilization of biomass and make recommendations based on the findings of this study. Population for the study was rural households and simple random sampling technique was employed in selecting six towns from the study area which include Amodu, Agbani, Ammuri, Ozalla, Obe, and Umueze, Ten household were randomly selected from the six selected towns. Data was collected from primary sources by the use of well-structured and validated questionnaires and a face to face interview. The data was analyzed using descriptive statistics which largely involves the use of frequencies, percentages, and 4 point likert type scale mean rating. Results show that about 75% of the respondents are female, the mean age is 46.03, about 66.7% were married, and an average educational level. In addition 45% of respondents were traders; the mean household size is 5.27, the mean number of years spent in the community by the respondents is 24.52 and the mean income is Nl41000 indicating that majority of the respondents earn an average income per month. The study also shows that the biomass used in the study area includes fuel, charcoal and crop residue (palm fronds, palm kernel seeds and chaff). Households acquire their biomass by collecting and purchasing their biomass from the forest, market, farm and their immediate environment, also the rated distance is on the averageIn addition, results also reveals that the rural households on the average use their biomass often for cooking only because they alternatively use other source of energy suck as kerosene, LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) and electricity for heating and lighting. The research also exposes the fact that 99% of the household have access to biomass and they use it as their source of fuel energy. Although the study investigated 14 possible constraints, but none was regarded as a 'major constraint to the household access and utilization of biomass. The study among other things recommends a more comprehensive effort to ensure efficient and sustainable use of biomass source of energy by rural households so as to avoid environmental degradation.

title: National Transformational Capacity Theory and the Integrated Economic Growth Model

detail.title: National Transformational Capacity Theory and the Integrated Economic Growth Model
detail.abstract: This article presents the National Transformational Capacity (NTC) Theory as an analytical framework for understanding the middle-income trap not merely as a problem of inadequate policies or scarce resources, but as a limitation in a country’s capacity to organize and strategically coordinate development at the system level. Building on this perspective, the paper links NTC to Vietnam’s Integrated Economic Growth Model (IGM) as a concrete application aimed at simultaneously addressing three structural bottlenecks of growth: low productivity, low domestic value added, and limited access to international markets. The analysis shows that Vietnam’s pathway toward high-quality growth depends on strengthening its national transformational capacity—turning reforms into endogenous drivers of development and opening a more sustainable long-term growth trajectory.

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between show-off culture and financial stress among young adults through a systematic theoretical review of existing literature. In the digital age, social media platforms have amplified conspicuous consumption and social comparison, shaping perceptions of success, lifestyle, and financial adequacy. The study draws upon established theories such as Veblen's Theory of Conspicuous Consumption, Social Comparison Theory, and concepts from Behavioral Finance to understand how digitally mediated social pressures influence financial behavior. Using secondary data from peer-reviewed journals, academic databases, and authoritative institutional reports, the study synthesizes key themes related to spending pressure, lifestyle inflation, credit dependence, and financial anxiety among young adults. The findings suggest that show-off culture, reinforced by social media visibility and validation mechanisms, contributes significantly to distorted financial decision-making and increased financial stress. The study highlights important implications for personal financial management, emphasizing the need for behavioral awareness and financial literacy that address psychological and social influences on spending behavior. By integrating financial and psychological perspectives, the paper contributes to a deeper theoretical understanding of social media-driven financial stress and identifies directions for future empirical research.

title: The Price of Market Fear: A Microstructure Analysis of Peru's Presidential Crisis (2016-2026)

detail.title: The Price of Market Fear: A Microstructure Analysis of Peru's Presidential Crisis (2016-2026)
detail.abstract: This paper challenges the conventional narrative that Peru's macroeconomic stability is decoupled from its chronic political instability. Analyzing a decade characterized by unprecedented executive turnover-eight presidents in ten years-we quantify the financial cost of governance crises using high-frequency microstructure data from 2016 to 2026. We construct a Synthetic Fear Index (VIX-PE) and utilize a generalized Garman-Kohlhagen specification adapted for endogenous interest rates to isolate "Market Fear" from broader societal insecurity. Our empirical results, based on 2,486 daily observations, reveal three structural findings. First, financial markets discriminate sharply between "executive noise" and "foundational risk." OLS regressions confirm that systemic risk peaked not during the chaotic tenure of Manuel Merino (β = 0.66), but during the 2021 electoral transition under Francisco Sagasti (β = 0.90 * * *), driven by the credible threat of constitutional change. Second, a scatter plot analysis identifies a distinct "Castillo Quadrant," characterized by high volatility and low liquidity. Third, applying the GK-Taylor option pricing model reveals a "Taylor Paradox": the implied cost of currency hedging remained at historical highs even as the Central Bank aggressively raised interest rates. We conclude that while the macroeconomic model survived, political instability imposed a severe "fear tax" on liquidity, rendering monetary transmission mechanisms less effective during periods of foundational uncertainty.

detail.abstract: Small inland municipalities in Brazil have faced significant long-term challenges related to productive specialization and limited economic diversification. São Pedro do Ivaí, located in the state of Paraná, experienced accelerated expansion during the mid-20th century, driven first by the coffee economy and later by the sugarcane industry. However, external shocks, particularly the 1975 frost, and structural dependency on a single agro-industrial activity have resulted in persistent socioeconomic stagnation. This paper analyzes the economic and demographic evolution of the municipality between 1970 and 2020, drawing on sectoral structure, specialization indices, and shift-share results. The findings reveal loss of competitiveness, decline in formal employment, aging population, and continuous out-migration of young workers. The case illustrates the vulnerability of small rural economies exposed to volatile agricultural markets and lacking endogenous drivers of innovation. These dynamics reflect broader regional challenges in Brazil's hinterland, emphasizing the need for diversification strategies and long-term territorial development policies aimed at strengthening resilience in small municipalities .

title: Mix Me the Perfect Stress Test
affiliations: Oliver Wyman

detail.title: Mix Me the Perfect Stress Test
detail.abstract: The success of stress testing to help end the Global Financial Crisis (GFC) motivated its inclusion in the post-GFC revisions to the regulatory capital regime. There is no perfect stress test design, but there are some desirable features: A) Multiple scenarios: One scenario is simply not enough to cover the space of relevant risks. B) Horizon length and time-step: Three-year scenarios using quarterly time-steps: to adequately capture different loss and revenue dynamics with acceptable model forecast deterioration, and to match financial reporting cadence. C) Models: Both banks and supervisors need to build their own set of models. D) Supervisor and bank (ICAAP): Supervisory (top-down) and bank (bottom up) stress tests, should be run simultaneously. E) How often: More is often better, but it is not costless. Annual for the largest and most complex banks, every other year for the next tier of banks. F) Disclosure: More is better, but because of strategic behavior, there can be too much disclosure. G) Exploratory scenarios and reverse stress testing: Both are excellent tools – supervisors should use them more extensively.

title: Easy Money? Refunding the Second Liberty Loan

detail.title: Easy Money? Refunding the Second Liberty Loan
detail.abstract: Upturning long-standing lore related to the ’easy money’ policy of the Federal Reserve Banks, this paper attributes the boom in U.S. stock prices that began in 1927 to the sudden redemption of the Second Liberty Loan. Described as ’one of the largest government operations conducted during peacetime,’ the Treasury’s programme for retiring the Second Liberty Loan not only unlocked a wall of reinvestment, which it steered into stocks by structurally-lowering the long-term rate, but also impressed itself on the monetary policy of the Federal Reserve Banks. Consistent with the Minsky-Kindleberger model, the argument is supported by the market displacement observed before the Tulip Bubble (1637), South Sea Bubble (1720), Mississippi Bubble (1720), Panic of 1825, Berlin Stock Market Bubble (1872), and Barings Crisis (1890).

detail.title: The Aggregate–Perception Divergence Theory An Ethological Theory of Human Economic Behavior
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Aggregate-Perception Divergence Theory (APDT) to explain the structural gap between improving macroeconomic indicators and deteriorating individual perceptions of stability. While institutional metrics (GDP, employment, aggregate safety) may signal systemic growth, subjective experience often reports heightened anxiety. We formalize individual perception (P_i) as a function of aggregate conditions modulated by perceived volatility, asymmetric risk exposure, and informational salience. This framework identifies a Perception Instability Equilibrium (PIE), where institutional stability and widespread subjective fragility coexist. The paper contributes to behavioral microeconomics by demonstrating how modern information density and risk asymmetry decouple statistical reality from perceived experience.

detail.title: The added value of an interdisciplinary academic primary care network in Belgium: a qualitative external evaluation using Soft Systems Methodology
detail.abstract: Be.Hive is an interdisciplinary academic chair in primary care in French-speaking Belgium that seeks to strengthen primary care by connecting research, teaching, practice, and policy. Created in 2019, it convenes universities, university colleges, primary care professionals, patient and caregiver organisations, and policy actors to address persistent fragmentation. This study evaluated the added value of Be.Hive as a social and organisational innovation, from the perspective of stakeholders outside its governance structures. We conducted a qualitative external evaluation using Soft Systems Methodology (SSM) to examine how Be.Hive is perceived, used, and valued. SSM informed the design of focus groups and collective sense-making workshops, supporting participants to articulate differing worldviews, surface tensions, and co-identify feasible improvements. Participants were representatives of professional platforms, policy administrations, patient and caregiver organisations, and meso-level support structures. Data were analysed iteratively using constant comparative methods. Stakeholders highlighted contributions in three interrelated domains: (1) capacity building through co-financing and mentoring of doctoral work anchored in primary care; (2) knowledge integration via participatory research, interdisciplinary workshops, and communities of practice linking academia, practitioners, and citizens; and (3) policy and system support through white papers, targeted analyses, and sustained engagement with regional and federal platforms. Reported challenges concerned role clarity, visibility, and alignment between expectations for system change and the boundaries of an academic mandate.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive critical analysis of the 2026 Bangladesh election manifestos from three major political parties: the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), the National Citizens Party (NCP), and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. The analysis examines each party's core agenda, identifies areas of cross-party consensus and divergence, and critically evaluates the feasibility of key promises. While all three parties demonstrate remarkable agreement on fundamental reforms-including justice for past atrocities, electoral system overhaul, anti-corruption measures, and universal healthcare-they differ significantly in their approaches to electoral architecture, constitutional identity, economic intervention, and foreign policy. The paper concludes by highlighting several ambitious commitments that appear impractical given current fiscal, administrative, and geopolitical constraints, raising important questions about the gap between electoral rhetoric and governance reality.

detail.abstract: Financial inclusion as a public good can be funded by the State and private firms to ensure that everyone has affordable access to formal financial services. Historically, the economic solution for financial inclusion has been to create public banks and issue banking license to private banks. Today, the solution for financial inclusion lies in offering public support to financial service providers to ensure that formal financial services is available and affordable so that everyone can access and use financial services to meet their needs. This article discusses the need to treat financial inclusion as a public good because financial inclusion is essential for the economic and social development of any nation. This article presents a detailed understanding of the public good theory of financial inclusion. title: Deciphering Hydrochemical Evolution, Source Apportionment, and Health Risk Prioritization in a Typical Arid/Semi-Arid Coal-Mining Area

detail.title: Deciphering Hydrochemical Evolution, Source Apportionment, and Health Risk Prioritization in a Typical Arid/Semi-Arid Coal-Mining Area
detail.abstract: In arid/semi-arid coal-mining regions, groundwater serves as the primary source for domestic, agricultural, and industrial water supply, yet its chemical composition is increasingly altered by intensive anthropogenic disturbances. A critical knowledge gap persists in quantitatively disentangling the coupled effects of natural hydrogeochemical evolution and multi-source anthropogenic inputs, and in translating this understanding into management-relevant risk prioritization. To address this issue, this study focused on the Huolingol mining area, a typical coal-mining region in Inner Mongolia, China, and integrated unsupervised machine learning (SOM), Entropy weight-technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution (EW-TOPSIS), positive matrix factorization (PMF), and Monte Carlo health risk simulation to construct a “hydrochemical differentiation-source apportionment-risk prioritization” framework. Groundwater samples were classified into three clusters: Na-HCO3/Ca-Na-HCO3 water dominated by intense cation exchange and silicate weathering (Cluster 1), Ca-Na-SO4/Ca-Na-HCO3 water influenced by anthropogenic contamination (Cluster 2), and Ca-HCO3 water representing the natural background (Cluster 3). Source apportionment using PMF revealed that human-driven composite pollution is the main cause of water quality evolution, with the mixed source of coal mine drainage and industrial/domestic wastewater contributing the highest proportion (22.42%), highlighting the overwhelming impact of mining and industrial activities. Health risk simulation indicated that groundwater contamination poses a more severe threat to children, whose probability of exceeding the non-carcinogenic risk threshold (33.9%) was considerably higher than that of adults (19.4%). F- and SO42- were identified as the primary risk-driving factors. By deciphering the “chemical fingerprint” and “risk code” of groundwater under intensive anthropogenic disturbance, this work provides a replicable paradigm for groundwater management in arid and semi-arid mining regions worldwide.

detail.abstract: Do large language models (LLMs) provide gender-neutral financial advice? We answer this question by prompting 33 widely used LLMs from five vendors, varying only a single word in otherwise identical prompts: "man" versus "woman." We find that women are advised to allocate 1.8 percentage points less to equity funds than men; this gap persists across vendors, model generations, and model complexity. Providing richer investor information attenuates but does not entirely eliminate the gender gap. Since even modest allocation differences imply persistent return differentials, algorithmic financial advice can shape wealth accumulation across demographic groups.

detail.abstract: This Insight examines how budgetary policy since 2011, a period of improved Irish economic performance after the crisis years of the late 2000s, has affected the income tax take and considers the impact of such changes on average tax rates across the income distribution. After the 2011 Budget, there were no noteworthy income tax changes until the mid-2010s. Thereafter, general income tax measures in Budgets have involved a reduction in the higher rate of income tax (from 41 per cent to 40 per cent in the 2015 Budget), increases in standard rate bands and personal and employee tax credits, and reductions in USC rates and changes in USC bands.

detail.abstract: This symposium issue seeks to harmonize international financial regulation by comparing and critiquing U.S. and EU approaches, including their convergences and divergences and the reasons therefor. To achieve this goal, the issue introduces a somewhat innovative approach: each article is co-authored by leading U.S. and EU financial regulation scholars. The divergences in the U.S. and EU financial regulatory frameworks might be explained, at least in part, by the differences in the structure of their financial systems: the United States is primarily market-based, whereas the European Union is largely bank-based. 1 For example, approximately 80% of corporate financing in the United States is funded through the capital markets, compared to only 30% in the European Union. 2 Another possible explanation for the divergences is that EU regulators and the European Central Bank have been more willing to impose top-down policy than their U.S. counterparts, which tend to rely more on voluntary, market-led efforts. Recognizing these differences, this symposium issue's comparative analyses should help the United States and the European Union learn from each other's regulatory successes and failures. That, in turn, should help identify "best practices" and increase regulatory efficiency. The comparative analyses should also further economic growth by increasing U.S. and EU regulatory convergence, building trust, and encouraging cross-border market access and business relationships. The demand for such cross-border access and business is increasingly critical with the expansion of crypto-assets and decentralized finance (DeFi), which transcend geographic boundaries. Regulatory convergence should also increase legal certainty, reduce regulatory risk, lower compliance costs, and facilitate more cooperative cross-border regulatory supervision. Additionally, such convergence could provide more common crisis responses to similar market failures, thereby reducing cross-border financial contagion.

detail.abstract: •  Notwithstanding some recent signs of stabilisation, Dublin’s office market has been amongst the hardest hit across Europe in terms of decrease in capital values, fall-off in investment and the rise in vacancy rates since the start of the decade. The extent of the slowdown, however, has not been as sharp as in some large US cities. Using an enhanced methodological framework to project short-run vacancy rates, the central scenario for the Dublin office vacancy rate is a marginal rise to just over 19 per cent in 2026 before falling back below end of 2024 levels (18.6 per cent) by the end of 2027. A scenario based on a more benign set of assumptions suggests that the Dublin office vacancy rate may have already peaked, while the more adverse case sees a return to levels last seen around the time of the Irish property market collapse in 2009. detail.title: Wins, Windfalls and Willpower: Liquidity and Self-Regulation in Online Sports Gambling
detail.abstract: We study how gambling behavior responds to prior-day outcomes, liquidity shocks, and bettors' awareness of potential harm, using betting data for a random sample of 24,453 online sports bettors. Relative to days with no resolved bets, bettors are 7 to 8 percentage points more likely to place a bet following either a win or a loss. Bettors increase their stake size after wins and shift toward higher-odds bets after losses. Liquidity windfalls from annual tax refunds do not affect the gambling participation rate, but lead to stake escalation among bettors vulnerable to gambling harm. Safe-gambling tools curb betting only when they directly limit engagement with the platform. Reminder-based awareness nudges, which notify bettors when their gambling expenditure or time spent on the gambling platform exceeds self-set limits, reduce participation but shift bets toward higher-risk wagers.

detail.abstract: This study explores the changing nature of work cultures in Kashmir through the lens of the gig economy, focusing on employment insecurity, digital platform governance and local labour realities. In a region marked by limited formal employment and recurring economic disruptions, platform-based gig work has emerged as a significant livelihood option for youth and informal workers. Using a qualitative research framework, the study adopted a non-probability sampling technique to collect primary data from 14 gig workers engaged in food and grocery, freelance work, teaching and taxi driving across urban centers of Kashmir. Semi-structured interviews were conducted to capture workers experiences, perceptions and coping strategies within platform-mediated employment. The collected data were systematically analyzed using NVivo 12 software, enabling thematic coding and interpretation. The findings reveal six major dimensions influencing gig workers experiences: income instability, platform control mechanisms, lack of social security, perceived flexibility of work, region-specific uncertainties and coping strategies. While gig work provides short-term income opportunities and autonomy over working hours, it simultaneously reinforces precarious employment conditions and deepens workers vulnerability. The study contributes to emerging research on digital labour and informal employment by situating the gig economy within Kashmir's unique socioeconomic context. It further highlights the need for region-sensitive labour policies, stronger regulatory frameworks, and inclusive social protection measures for gig workers.

title: AI Development, Energy Markets, and Macroeconomy: A Dynamic General Equilibrium Analysis

detail.title: AI Development, Energy Markets, and Macroeconomy: A Dynamic General Equilibrium Analysis
detail.abstract: This note quantifies the interplay between AI development, capital accumulation, and energy markets using a three-sector dynamic general equilibrium model calibrated to the Japanese economy. We analyze steady-state shifts driven by a 100 times increase in AI productivity. Our analysis yields four primary findings. First, while Real GDP expands to 2.5 times its initial level, household welfare gains are more modest because the AI-intensive economy necessitates a higher investment share at the expense of household consumption. Second, we identify a quantitative "Jevons paradox": while technological development enhances the energy efficiency of AI, the volume effect of AI demand and the resulting intensified energy consumption drive energy prices up by nearly 7 times. Third, the shift to the new AI-intensive economy induces a huge structural decline in the labor income share from 55% to 31%. Finally, these outcomes are highly sensitive to the elasticity of substitution between labor and AI; a 5% increase in the elasticity doubles the energy price response, highlighting the uncertainty inherent in the shift to an AI-driven era.

title: Are There Adverse Health Shocks at Social Security Eligibility Age?
