detail.title: Are There Adverse Health Shocks at Social Security Eligibility Age?
detail.abstract: I use a regression discontinuity design to investigate the causal relationships between the Earliest Eligibility Age (EEA) for Social Security of 62, retirement, and health in the U.S. I use data from the Health and Retirement Study to explore these relationships. I find that, at the EEA, the probability of receiving Social Security benefits increases by 23 to 29 percentage points. There exists some evidence that the probability of being currently retired among males rises by 8 to 12 percentage points at the EEA. However, I do not find much evidence that the EEA has impacts, especially detrimental impacts, on health. These findings imply that it is difficult to generalize the findings of Fitzpatrick and Moore (2018) that adverse health shocks caused by retirement at the EEA lead to an increase in age-in-months mortality counts immediately after the EEA to the whole population of the U.S. elderly.

title: The Influence Of Cooperatives On Capacity Building And Capabilities Of Members

detail.title: The Influence Of Cooperatives On Capacity Building And Capabilities Of Members
detail.abstract: Cooperatives are people's economic institutions that play a strategic role in improving the welfare of members through strengthening individual and collective capacities and capabilities. Member capacity includes increasing knowledge, technical, managerial, and entrepreneurial skills, while capabilities relate to the ability to make decisions, adapt to changes in the economic environment, and act independently in economic activities. This paper aims to conceptually examine the influence of cooperatives on the development of member capacity and capability and examine the institutional mechanisms that support the empowerment of members in a sustainable manner. The discussion focused on the role of cooperatives in providing economic services, encouraging member participation, developing human resources, strengthening social solidarity, and improving internal governance. The method used is literature review, by analyzing books, journal articles, policy reports, and other relevant scientific publications. The results of the study show that cooperatives contribute significantly to improving the technical, managerial, and entrepreneurial capabilities of members, while strengthening the independence, adaptability, decision-making capacity, and responsiveness of members to market dynamics. Cooperatives not only function as economic entities, but also as a means of empowering members in a sustainable manner, expanding individual capabilities, and supporting inclusive economic development. This paper is expected to provide a comprehensive conceptual understanding of the role of cooperatives and serve as a reference for the development of policies, institutional practices, and member empowerment strategies in the future.

title: Can Market Mechanisms Solve the Refugee Crisis?

detail.title: Can Market Mechanisms Solve the Refugee Crisis?
detail.abstract: Ever since the major inflow of refugees (the “refugee crisis”) in 2015 and 2016, there has been heated debate about the appropriate distribution of refugees in the EU. Current policies revolve around mandatory quotas, which disregard the preferences of EU members and refugees alike. This problem can be addressed with two market mechanisms. First, tradable quotas minimize the cost of asylum provision for host countries. Second, a matching system gives refugees more discretion over where they are sheltered. While this proposal is theoretically appealing, it has yet to be tested in practice.

title: On the Cost Dynamics in Multimorbid Individuals: A Quantile Regression Analysis of Insurance Claims

detail.title: On the Cost Dynamics in Multimorbid Individuals: A Quantile Regression Analysis of Insurance Claims
detail.abstract: Multimorbidity, the co-occurrence of multiple chronic conditions, places a substantial economic burden on health systems, particularly due to increased healthcare utilization and complex cost interactions in older adults. Traditional cost models often focus on individual diseases, failing to account for the compounded effects of multimorbidity, which can lead to non-linear increases in costs. In this study, we analyze health insurance claims from 313,257 policyholders (2014-2022) to model cost variations across morbidity states, disease groups, age, and gender. We identify distinct phases based on cost patterns and apply quantile regression within a gradient boosting machine framework to estimate conditional cost distributions. Our results show a sublinear increase in median costs with advancing multimorbidity and significantly lower costs in the treatment phase compared to the initial months after diagnosis. While cancer, immune disorders, and HIV incur the highest initial monthly costs, hypertension poses the greatest total economic burden due to its high prevalence. These findings provide a more refined understanding of multimorbidity-related cost dynamics, informing actuarial reserving, pricing, resource allocation, and targeted interventions.

title: Market Volatility and the Warsh Nomination An Expectations-Driven Monetary Shock

detail.abstract: Recent financial market volatility following the nomination of Kevin Warsh to a prominent role at the Federal Reserve reflects an expectations-driven monetary shock rather than a structural economic crisis. This article interprets the episode using standard macroeconomic frameworks, emphasizing the role of monetary credibility, inflation expectations, and openeconomy transmission mechanisms. The episode illustrates how financial markets respond immediately to credible policy signals, while real economic adjustments occur with substantial lags.

detail.title: Bond funds’ risk taking and monetary policy
detail.abstract: Using granular security-level data from bond funds domiciled in the US and the euro area, we identify a market-based risk-taking channel of monetary policy transmission via the credit-risk and the maturity structure of bond funds’ portfolios. We measure credit risk at the fund level as the weighted average credit rating of the fund’s bond holdings. We find that accommodative monetary policies by the Fed and the ECB are associated with increased risk in bond funds’ portfolios. Interestingly, risk-taking is more pronounced for funds with longer-term holdings relative to short-term ones and unconventional monetary policy exerts stronger market-based risk-taking effects than interest rate policy. Finally, we find that Fed’s monetary policy has a stronger impact on funds’ risk-taking behaviour than the ECB’s, highlighting the dominant role of US monetary policy in global financial markets.

detail.abstract:
This theoretical framework introduces the Systemic Socio-Spatial Rhythms Theory as an innovative relational-temporal approach to contemporary social geography. The theory addresses critical gaps in traditional geographic analysis by repositioning rhythm as the fundamental organizing principle of socio-spatial life. Drawing upon Henri Lefebvre's rhythmanalysis, Doreen Massey's relational geography, complexity theory, and temporal sociology, this approach transcends conventional space-time dichotomies by conceptualizing social spaces as polyrhythmic systems constituted through intersecting temporal-spatial processes operating simultaneously at multiple scales.

The theory rests on five core features: (1) interwoven spatio-temporal rhythmicity that treats space and time as inseparable dimensions manifesting as rhythm; (2) dynamic systemic relationality emphasizing open systems of interactive relationships; (3) polyrhythmia and spatial polyphony recognizing the coexistence of multiple distinct rhythms within shared spaces; (4) emergence and non-linear complexity whereby rhythmic interactions generate irreducible spatial patterns; and (5) critical transformativity that exposes power relations embedded in rhythmic arrangements while identifying possibilities for emancipatory change.

The methodological operationalization integrates quantitative formalization through a comprehensive Systemic Socio-Spatial Rhythmic Index (SSRI) with multi-method field protocols including structured rhythmic observations, time-space diary surveys, biographical rhythm interviews, and digital trace analysis. This mixed-methods approach enables rigorous empirical investigation while preserving attention to lived experience, power dynamics, and transformative possibilities.

The theoretical and methodological contributions address contemporary challenges including social acceleration, globalization's rhythmic impacts, platform economy temporalities, climate disruption of established seasonal patterns, and hybrid physical-digital rhythms. Applications span urban planning, rural transformation studies, migration and transnational rhythms, and environmental sustainability. By foregrounding rhythm as simultaneously an analytical category and a political terrain, this framework offers tools for understanding how temporal-spatial arrangements serve particular interests while opening pathways toward more just and democratic rhythmic orders.

This approach represents a paradigm shift in social geography, moving from static spatial analysis toward dynamic understanding of how spaces are continuously produced and reproduced through rhythmic practices, how multiple temporalities interact to generate emergent spatial patterns, and how rhythmic struggles constitute fundamental sites of social contestation and transformation.

title: The Unified Principle: A Structural Framework for Foundational Mathematical and Computational Problems

detail.title: The Unified Principle: A Structural Framework for Foundational Mathematical and Computational Problems
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Unified Principle (UP), an axiomatic framework designed to provide a coherent structural foundation for multiple longstanding mathematical and computational problems. The framework interprets classical challenges in terms of discrete indexing, orthogonality, and invariant-preserving cyclic correction, allowing them to be reformulated within a unified structural system. Problems considered include the P versus NP problem, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, Yang-Mills existence and mass gap, the Hodge Conjecture, the Riemann Hypothesis, the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture, and the Poincaré Conjecture, as well as select additional number-theoretic, combinatorial, and topological conjectures. Within the UP, computational problems such as P versus NP are framed as questions of orthogonality between solution discovery and verification, whereas physical and topological problems are interpreted as constraints on invariant-preserving evolution and cyclic closure. The framework establishes a formal language and operator set applicable across these domains, enabling consistent structural analysis and comparison. While this manuscript does not present formal proofs, it demonstrates how a single axiomatic system can host and structurally unify multiple foundational problems, providing a basis for future formal development and investigation.

detail.abstract: How is it that, despite its rich and unique biodiversity, Campo Ma'an National Park contributes so little to economic development and its integrity is so severely threatened by poaching, encroachment, and land grabbing? This situation has led to a debate over whether to maintain the park's current status or convert it. Cost-benefit analysis (CBA) provides a theoretical basis and relevant and objective comparison tools for choosing between the options of exploitation and conservation of natural resources, through the calculation of total economic value (TEV). TEV represents the diversity of economic benefits that a conserved natural asset can provide to the human community. The annual TEV (TEVa) of the park for the conservation scenario was estimated at USD 77,712,710, while the TEVa of the park favorable to exploitation was calculated at USD 77,105,472. The relative advantage of TEW for conservation over exploitation can be explained by the low contribution of tourism to the local and regional economy, the low financial contribution to conservation, and the conflictual relationships between stakeholders. The study revealed that local communities (94%) are more interested in the park for its economic benefits and show less interest in conservation, believing that their activities pose less of a threat to the environment than those of other stakeholders. Furthermore, 93.37% of the people surveyed are in favor of converting the park for development, provided that only social or community projects are implemented, such as the creation of a communal forest, the construction of a dam, a port, a road, etc.

title: The Data Trap: When AI Fails
affiliations: Tsinghua University - Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management, Tsinghua University - Institute of Economics and Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management

detail.title: The Data Trap: When AI Fails
detail.abstract: We model the co-evolution of AI and the economy using a task-based dynamic framework where data quality is an endogenous variable. In our model, next-generation AI capability is a function of training data quantity and quality. The data pool mixes real data from economic activity with synthetic data from incumbent AI. The automation process itself also generates partially synthetic data, creating a data-AI feedback loop. Our analysis shows this mechanism can lead to two traps from different perspectives. First, a development trap may arise in the steadystate. An over-reliance on synthetic data can degrade quality, trapping the economy into a long-run equilibrium with lower automation and output. Second, the system can fall into a dynamic trap of persistent boom-bust cycles. Instability in the feedback loop can prevent convergence, trapping the economy in oscillations that may evolve through period-doubling bifurcations into chaos. We then examine policy responses. A countercyclical levy on synthetic-data use, indexed to model performance or output, stabilizes endogenous cycles without depressing long-run levels. Caps on the synthetic share work in the same direction, while AI adoption caps may be counterproductive by reducing real-data generation. A complementary source-side policy is public investment in data infrastructure that expands the supply of high-quality real data, albeit subject to a crowding-out trade-off in production labor. These results highlight the importance of protecting the information environment and sustaining high-quality real data.

title: Capital Allocation and Community Resilience: Examining Market Investment in Socially Beneficial Projects

detail.title: Capital Allocation and Community Resilience: Examining Market Investment in Socially Beneficial Projects
detail.abstract: This paper discusses the way capital is allocated in a market, and how this relates to the resilience of a community and whether or not there is residual under-investment in projects with significant positive 'social spillover'. Markets, per se, give primary consideration to the perceived private returns which could result in certain endeavors that could serve the greater good not being sufficiently funded because the perceived returns to the investor are limited. The resilience of a community is defined as its ability to 'absorb, adapt and transform' after experiencing a shock, and whether investment can be targeted to develop this within a local economy; particularly in investments in projects that have a positive effect beyond those who directly utilize and pay for them. And whether the biases evident in market systems mean certain projects that would incur significant positive 'social spillover' are consistently under-invested in. The paper, therefore, attempts to integrate some of the more established economic theories with real-life examples in order to demonstrate the effects of capital allocation in a market and its effects on society.

title: The Politics of Nostalgia: How Digital Media Revives, Reinvents, and Polarises National Memory in India

detail.title: The Politics of Nostalgia: How Digital Media Revives, Reinvents, and Polarises National Memory in India
detail.abstract: This paper explores the complex role of nostalgia in shaping national memory in contemporary India, with a particular focus on how digital media platforms amplify, reinvent, and polarise historical narratives. Drawing on cultural memory studies, media theory, and recent examples from social media, the paper argues that nostalgia is neither inherently conservative nor progressive, but rather functions as a contested space where multiple identities and political agendas converge. In the Indian context, digital nostalgia surfaces in diverse forms: from romanticised portrayals of ancient empires to grassroots rediscoveries of neglected regional figures and communities. While such narratives can foster cultural pride and inclusivity, they can equally fuel exclusionary identity politics and historical grievance. The study shows how algorithmic amplification and emotionally charged content simplify complex histories into shareable, polarised stories, contributing to both empowerment and division. Ultimately, the paper suggests that nostalgia, when critically engaged, can serve not only as a bridge to the past but also as a tool for a more reflective national conversation about belonging, history, and identity.

title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Trade in the Short Run: An Empirical Investigation of the Reciprocal Tarif

detail.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Trade in the Short Run: An Empirical Investigation of the Reciprocal Tarif
detail.abstract: This paper examines the short run effects of trade policy uncertainty (TPU) arising from the U.S. Reciprocal Tariff announcement. Using monthly import data, we find that U.S. firms increased imports from countries facing higher TPU. Contrary to conventional views that TPU suppresses trade, our results highlight a distinct short run importer response consistent with recent inventory management theories. This study offers one of the first empirical assessments of the Reciprocal Tariff's impact and contributes to understanding how firms react to trade policy uncertainty in the short term.

title: Talent War, Financial Development, and Income Inequality
affiliations: Hunan Normal University,  and Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

detail.title: Talent War, Financial Development, and Income Inequality
detail.abstract: We exploit a unique policy change – Talent War Policy – implemented in 231 cities in China between 2016 and 2018 as an empirical setting to study the impact of large influx of skilled labor on local financial development and income inequality. We find that relative to the control group, cities that implement Talent War Policies experience significant increases in population, migrants, uses of digitized banking products, venture capital investments, and IPOs. These results are particularly pronounced for cities with higher degree of economic development, cities with greater higher education presence, cities with higher living cost, and cities with greater employment protection. However, talent War Policies seem to also lead to increased income disparity between urban and rural areas, resulting in a greater Theil Index.

title: Artificial Intelligence And Copyright Laws: A Critical Analysis Of Challenges And Legal Adaptations
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence And Copyright Laws: A Critical Analysis Of Challenges And Legal Adaptations
detail.abstract: In today's rapidly evolving world, artificial intelligence has gained remarkable capabilities and has led to numerous breakthroughs across different sectors, such as health, games, education, and entertainment. Intellectual Property Law is one of them. Artificial intelligence is both a product and a result of human innovation. Just like human behavior and cognitive processes, artificial intelligence has transformed machines into entities that resemble humans in our society. Prof Stephen Hawking once said that "the development of full artificial intelligence could spell the end of the human race". He further said that "it would take off on its own, and redesign itself at an ever-increasing rate" and "humans, who are limited by slow biological evolution, couldn't compete, and would be superseded" 1. As artificial intelligence continues to advance, intellectual property rights have introduced complex legal challenges. AI is shifting the limits of human creativity and technological advancement in the realm of Copyright, encompassing everything from poetry generation to music composition and novel writing. Intellectual property rights are the rights given to persons over the creations of their minds. They usually give the creator an exclusive right over the use of their creation for a certain period. 2 These rights play an important role in promoting innovation and creativity, protecting individuals who are the original creators, and imposing a legal obligation on them. There are various types of IPR, including copyright, trademark, patent, trade secret, geographical indication, and plant variety rights. Copyright protects the author's original wor,k such as literary, artistic, dramatic, and musical works. It includes books, pictures, movies, and songs. This work is protected for a particular period, i.e., the life of the author + 60 years. Copyright also provides broadcasting rights to reproduce, distribute, perform, and display their work.

title: Impact of Earnings Surprises on Short-Term Asset Price Momentum

detail.title: Impact of Earnings Surprises on Short-Term Asset Price Momentum
detail.abstract: Earnings surprises, which are instances where a company's reported earnings deviate from consensus analyst expectations, are among the most potent catalysts for short-term asset price movements in equity markets. This report provides a comprehensive, evidence-based analysis of how positive and negative earnings surprises affect stock prices in the days immediately following earnings announcements. Drawing on classic and contemporary academic literature, recent empirical data (including 2024-2026 market evidence), and sectoral and firmsize heterogeneity, the report explores the mechanisms underlying post-announcement price momentum, including investor underreaction, information diffusion, and behavioral biases. Methodological approaches such as event studies, regression models, and portfolio tests are discussed in detail, alongside the latest advances in measuring earnings surprises. The report also examines the role of market conditions, sectoral dynamics, and firm characteristics in shaping the magnitude and persistence of post-earnings momentum. Policy implications, practical trading strategies, and avenues for future research are addressed, providing a holistic view of this enduring market anomaly.

title: Future (of) Trade Mark Functions

detail.title: Future (of) Trade Mark Functions

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming in I Fhima and A Moerland (eds), Research Agendas in Trade Mark Law (Edward Elgar 2026)

detail.abstract:
This chapter proposes that a research agenda for the coming years is more productively framed in terms of the future of trade mark functions. Rather than attempting to exhaustively define existing functions or predict others that may (never) come into existence, recent developments steer the debate in another direction. In particular, recent CJEU judgments situate the functions doctrine within a movement of lateral expansion subsuming market practices such as debranding and spare vehicle parts - practices that do not involve the actual use of a mark and were generally thought to fall outside the realm of European trade mark law. This move should reorient the discussion towards developing trade mark functions as an overarching, externally coherent doctrine capable of (de)limiting the scope of protection.

The future of trade mark functions is entwined with the quintessential question of reconciling trade mark law with normative concerns and other societal interests affected by exclusionary rights granted through registration. Part of the answer – or at least a promising starting point – may reside in a more meaningful and clear engagement with the notion of actionable harm.

title: Reimagining Public Sector Compensation in the 21st Century: A Policy Analysis of the 8th Central Pay Commission Questionnaire
affiliations: Kuvempu University

detail.title: Reimagining Public Sector Compensation in the 21st Century: A Policy Analysis of the 8th Central Pay Commission Questionnaire
detail.abstract: The 8th Central Pay Commission (CPC) of India, questionnaire signals a decisive shift from routine pay revision toward a broader re-examination of government compensation as an instrument of economic and governance policy. Rather than focusing solely on salary enhancement, the questions frame public pay within macroeconomic constraints, fiscal sustainability, labour-market dynamics, and long-term pension liabilities. The questionnaire reflects global public-sector reform trends, including assessment of total compensation instead of cash pay alone, reconsideration of uniform pay structures, sector-specific benchmarking, and differentiated career progression to attract and retain talent. It also highlights emerging concerns such as the signalling effect of government wages on informal and gig-sector compensation, the sustainability of pension systems amid a rising retiree population, and the relevance of hybrid indexation models for dearness allowance in a low-inflation environment. Overall, the 8th CPC appears to be exploring a calibrated and internationally informed redesign of India’s public sector compensation framework, seeking to balance employee expectations with fiscal prudence, economic stability, and the evolving requirements of 21st-century public administration.

title: US Military Hegemony and the Global Price of Risk
affiliations: University of Arizona

detail.title: US Military Hegemony and the Global Price of Risk
detail.abstract: This paper studies how U.S. fiscal policy transmits internationally and why its effects vary systematically across countries and asset classes. I document that country-level asset betas with respect to U.S. fiscal--military shocks exhibit large cross-sectional heterogeneity across sovereign bonds, equities, and currencies, and that this heterogeneity is tightly linked to the U.S. military presence. Countries that are more reliant on US military assistance experience stronger US fiscal transmission, higher equity and bond risk premia, and currencies that appreciate in adverse U.S. fiscal states. To interpret these patterns, I develop a multi-country general equilibrium model in which U.S. fiscal policy transmits through the US security umbrella: the system of security guarantees that the US extends to allied nations. This system of fiscal insurance links together US military spending, allied fiscal behavior, sovereign default risk, and international financial wedges. A quantitative extension shows that the model matches the magnitude and cross-sectional structure of US fiscal betas and factor-mimicking portfolios across asset classes, highlighting U.S. military insurance as a central determinant of global risk premia.

title: Who Profits from Prediction Markets? Execution, not Information
affiliations: The University of San Diego - Knauss School of Business

detail.title: Who Profits from Prediction Markets? Execution, not Information
detail.abstract: Retail traders correctly forecast asset price direction yet lose money. Using 222 million prediction market trades with observable terminal payoffs, we decompose returns into a directional component (did the trader pick the right side?) and an execution component (did the trader get a favorable price?). Traders with above-random accuracy earn negative returns because they arrive late and pay unfavorable prices; traders with near-random accuracy profit through superior execution. These two dimensions of skill are nearly orthogonal (ρ ≈ 0.13), and split-sample tests confirm both are persistent. What separates profitable from unprofitable traders is not forecasting ability but execution: automated traders pay 2.52 cents less per contract than casual traders, and this gap alone accounts for the sign of returns across trader types. Being right and making money are not the same thing.

title: International Financial Soft Law and Insurance Supervision
affiliations: University of Zurich - Rechtswissenschaftliches Institut (School of Law)

detail.title: International Financial Soft Law and Insurance Supervision
detail.abstract: This paper examines the theoretical framework of international soft law and how it embraces both legally nonbinding and binding rules and standards of international insurance regulation. International soft law is defined as legally nonbinding standards, principles, and rules that influence and shape state behavior but do not fit into the traditional categories of public international law, such as customary international law and bilateral or multilateral agreements or treaties. Binding international legal rules govern only limited areas of the international financial system. Most of the international rules, guidelines, standards, and other arrangements that govern financial regulation are not of a legally binding nature and are therefore generally referred to as "international financial soft law". This paper analyses the conceptual basis of international financial soft law in insurance regulation by considering the standards and principles adopted by the International Association of Insurance Supervisors.

title: DeFi vs. TradFi: Institutions and Industrial Organization
affiliations: University of Toronto

detail.title: DeFi vs. TradFi: Institutions and Industrial Organization

declarations.funderStatement: The paper was sponsored by the Wharton Institute for Policy Research.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the institutional and organizational differences between traditional finance and decentralized finance (DeFi), with a focus on public, permissionless blockchains. In traditional markets, intermediaries provide custody, authentication, settlement, and regulatory compliance. By contrast, the option of self-custody and open access on blockchains fundamentally reshapes the organization of financial services and challenges the foundations of current regulatory approaches. These structural differences alter trading, lending, and derivatives markets while introducing risks such as smart contract failures and infrastructure concentration. At the same time, DeFi's openness reduces entry barriers, improves transparency and access, and fosters competition and efficiency. Because self-custody removes intermediaries as enforcement points, regulation cannot simply extend existing frameworks. I conclude with policy recommendations emphasizing self-custody rights, privacy protection, adaptive regulation, and integration pathways for traditional intermediaries.

title: Information Design in Market Queuing Systems
affiliations: Cornell University

detail.title: Information Design in Market Queuing Systems
detail.abstract: We develop a game-theoretic framework that compares welfare efficiency across three market mechanisms: continuous double auctions with transparent order books (lit exchanges), opaque order books (dark pools), and periodic batch auctions. Each mechanism is modeled as a queuing system where heterogeneous traders face trade-offs between the execution price, waiting costs, and transaction costs. Our main result establishes that under moderate arrival rates and bounded adverse selection, dark pools dominate both alternatives in aggregate ex-ante welfare. Observable order books create costly strategic timing games in which traders delay or rush submissions to optimize the position of the queue, generating wasteful social waiting costs. Opaque order books eliminate these timing games through information design. We formally characterize the equilibrium strategies in each mechanism and prove the welfare ranking W DARK > W LIT > W BAT CH. Extensions incorporate asymmetric information and endogenous venue choice. The results demonstrate how the information structure and the discipline of the service jointly determine efficiency in strategic matching environments.

title: Open Questions | Yuen Yuen Ang on How China Can Turn "Polycrisis" Into "Polytunity"
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University

detail.title: Open Questions | Yuen Yuen Ang on How China Can Turn "Polycrisis" Into "Polytunity"

contentFormat.other: Media interview article posted for academic reference with content waiver from the South China Morning Post.

detail.abstract: In this interview, Yuen Yuen Ang argues that many US narratives about China oscillate between extremes (“collapse” vs “take over”) and often reflect America’s self-perception more than China’s underlying realities. Ang explains China’s reform-era political economy as “directed improvisation”: central authorities set broad direction, while local governments and entrepreneurs adapt pragmatically on the ground, producing diverse regional models. In today’s shift from export/real-estate-led growth to innovation-driven development, this approach persists but faces new limits because innovation is uncertain and hard to measure; KPI-style targets (e.g., patents) can be gamed, prompting iterative policy correction. Ang highlights parallels with the US model of “coordinated decentralization,” emphasizing that effective governance in the innovation age is more about directing ecosystems than dictating outcomes. She reframes today’s “polycrisis” as “polytunity,” stressing that a crumbling, unequal global order also creates openings for fairer alternatives and greater agency for developing countries.

title: The Southern Paradox: Community Norms and the Justification of Intimate Partner Violence in India
affiliations: Indian Institute of Technology, Hyderabad, Plaksha University and Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad

detail.title: The Southern Paradox: Community Norms and the Justification of Intimate Partner Violence in India
detail.abstract: Conventional empowerment theories suggest that women in more developed regions should be less likely to justify Intimate Partner Violence (IPV). In India, however, a stark paradox emerges. Our analytical sample reveals that women in the more developed Southern states are dramatically more likely to justify IPV (77.4%) compared to women in the rest of India (37.6%). This study investigates the drivers of this "Southern Paradox" using nonlinear decomposition methods on a national sample of 56,421 currently married women. The analysis quantifies how much of the regional gap is explained by differences in observed characteristics (endowments) versus differences in the returns to those characteristics (coefficients). The decomposition analysis shows a striking finding: differences in individual empowerment indicators like education and wealth explain very little of the gap. Instead, the vast majority of the explained regional difference is attributable to a single factor: higher average IPV justification at the neighbourhood level (62.6%). These findings demonstrate that powerful neighbourhood-level norms can override the protective effects of individual empowerment, suggesting that policy interventions must directly target collective attitudes to successfully combat the normalization of violence.

detail.abstract: In an age of interconnected crises, this paper introduces the Sustainable Development Resilience Index (SDRI) as a novel composite tool to gauge Germany's long-term sustainability and adaptive capacity from 1990 to 2023. Drawing on the ECON-ESG framework, the index integrates 14 indicators across economic (30%), social (25%), environmental (25%), and governance (20%) pillars, normalized via min-max methods and imputed conservatively for transparency. Empirical analysis reveals a trajectory of progress peaking at medium-high resilience around 2014-2015, followed by a decline amid energy shocks and social vulnerabilities. Using ARDL cointegration modeling robustified with OLS and GMM key drivers emerge: GDP growth, renewable energy, R&D, and trade openness enhance resilience, while inflation, CO₂ emissions, and FDI inflows hinder it. These insights underscore the need for integrated policies to foster adaptive transformations, offering a practical dashboard for policymakers navigating polycrises toward equitable, enduring development.

title: Food Choice Architecture: An Experimental Study
affiliations: , Lingnan University - Department of Economics and Peking University - HSBC School of Business

detail.title: Food Choice Architecture: An Experimental Study
detail.abstract: Despite the widespread application of choice architecture strategies, direct evidence comparing their effectiveness and heterogeneity in a common setting remains limited. In this study, we conduct a randomized controlled experiment to examine the effects of six choice architecture strategies, alongside a financial incentive, on promoting healthier food choices. We find that certain choice architecture strategies generate economically meaningful effects, though generally weaker than those of financial incentives. Offering half portions at full price yields the largest reductions in calorie and fat intake, by 13-14%, while healthy defaults and calorie labeling increase fruit selection by 9-12% and reduce calorie and fat intake by 7-12%. Causal-forest estimates of heterogeneous treatment effect reveal that the effectiveness ranking of interventions is highly stable across individuals. In the experiment, we also frame some interventions reversely to promote less healthy choices, and the effects turn out to be symmetric with those of the interventions to promote healthier choices. This finding, together with the high consistency of individual-level responses across interventions, highlights that behavioral malleability is an important trait for understanding the mechanism of choice architecture.

title: The Invisible Elements of GDP: How Much do They Matter in International Comparisons?

detail.title: The Invisible Elements of GDP: How Much do They Matter in International Comparisons?
detail.abstract: Gross domestic product (GDP) plays a central role in international comparisons, assessments of competitiveness, and economic policymaking. Yet national accounts systematically understate the contribution of two increasingly important sources of economic value: data and public services. Data, the essential capital asset of the data-driven economy, is recorded largely on a cost basis that excludes the substantial economic rents it generates, while its role in barter-like exchanges for “free” digital services remains invisible in trade statistics. Public services are similarly valued at cost, obscuring cross-country differences in the effectiveness of governance and the welfare gains it delivers. This paper argues that these omissions distort international GDP and trade comparisons, bias policy choices toward private over public goods, and risk misjudgments in trade negotiations. Using Canada–United States comparisons, the paper illustrates how invisible data rents understate US economic advantages while the unmeasured value of public services – proxied by life-expectancy differentials – substantially understates Canada’s economic performance. These measurement deficiencies not only distort public perceptions of comparative economic performance but have direct implications for resource allocation motivated by competitiveness concerns, and data-related commitments in the upcoming CUSMA review.

By examining geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions, and shifts in global supply chains, the study argues that globalisation has not declined but has evolved into a more diversified and resilient form. Evidence from global trade volumes, capital flows, and digital connectivity supports the conclusion that the global economy remains fundamentally interconnected.

title: Wool Cortisol Concentration as a Measure of Chronic Stress in Grazing Sheep
affiliations: University of Namur, University of Namur, University of Namur, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Namur and University of Namur

detail.title: Wool Cortisol Concentration as a Measure of Chronic Stress in Grazing Sheep
detail.abstract: Dual use of lands for renewable energy and animals grazing raises concerns regarding animal welfare. The visual environment is modified by the presence of solar panels rows, which could contribute to impaired visual contact, social stress and reduced expression of normal behaviors. Wool cortisol concentration has been described as biomarker of chronic stress as cortisol accumulates in growing wool fibers overtime. We hypothesized that wool cortisol concentration would differ in sheep grazing on solar parcel compared to those grazing on control parcel. Forty French Texel ewes were randomly allocated to either solar grazing (N= 20) or conventional grazing parcels (N=20) for 70 days during Fall 2023. Rams were introduced for a 35-day period. The primary outcome was wool cortisol concentration, measured in regrown wool during grazing period. Reproductive performance at ultrasound (35 days after ram removal), mating monitoring, blood work, cortisolemia and body condition score were secondary outcomes. Wool cortisol concentration did not differ between grazing conditions. Secondary outcomes were within physiological reference ranges, and supported the results of wool cortisol measurements. Limitations of the study include the modest number of animals (limited by parcels size and stocking density constraints) and the short-term follow-up. Wool cortisol concentration was low in both grazing types and did not differ between groups.

title: The Post‑Pandemic Global R
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York and Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York

detail.title: The Post‑Pandemic Global R

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
In this post we provide a measure of “global” r* using data on short- and long-term yields and inflation for several countries with the approach developed in “Global Trends in Interest Rates” (Del Negro, Giannone, Giannoni, and Tambalotti). After declining significantly from the 1990s to before the COVID-19 pandemic, global r* has risen but remains well below its pre-1990s level. These conclusions are based on an econometric model called "trendy VAR" that extracts common trends across a multitude of variables. Specifically, the common trend in real rates across all the countries in the sample is what we call global r*. The post is based on the discussion of an insightful paper by Lukasz Rachel on the drivers of r* presented at the Brookings Papers on Economic Activity Fall 2025 conference.

title: Economic Revitalisation through Diversification and Innovation: A Pathway to Sustainable Growth
affiliations: Nnamdi Azikiwe University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Economic Revitalisation through Diversification and Innovation: A Pathway to Sustainable Growth
detail.abstract: ln the face of persistent global shocks and deep-seated structural clogs, economic revitalisation has emerged as a critical priority for developing countries seeking to restore growth and build long-term resilence. This study examines economic revitalisation with meaningful, sustainable growth anchored on diversification, driven by disruptive innovations. Nigeria is among the largest economies in Africa, but it offers limited opportunities to most of its citizens. Its potential for greatness is not in doubt, given its abundant human and natural resources. However, Nigeria operates as a mono-economy, primarily dependent on crude oil exports for most of its earnings. This reliance has resulted in dire consequences for Nigeria's economy, even though the economic managers do have strategies and plans, which include, among other things, economic revitalisation. Some consequences are evident through a steady increase in the unemployment rate and debt accumulation, an increase in the poverty rate, inequality, corruption, other social vices, and a continuous decline in human capital development. All these factors result in unsustainable economic growth. Hence, this study recommends, among other things, the economic diversification by leveraging disruptive innovation for sustainable growth.

title: Enterprise Risk Management and Firm Resilience to External Shocks: Evidence from the COVID-19 Pandemic
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Saint Mary's University, Canada - Sobey School of Business, University of Calgary - Haskayne School of Business and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Enterprise Risk Management and Firm Resilience to External Shocks: Evidence from the COVID-19 Pandemic
detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has renewed scholarly attention regarding whether Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) enhances firm resilience under conditions of extreme uncertainty. This study examines whether ERM experience influences firm resilience during the COVID-19 shock. Drawing on the theory of dynamic capability, we conceptualize ERM as an experience-based capability that enables firms to better absorb exogenous shocks by strengthening coordination, information processing, and strategic responsiveness. Using a large panel of 2,909 U.S. publicly listed firms, we apply a modified machine-learning approach (the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) algorithm) to identify ERM adoption and maturity and employ a difference-in-differences design that exploits the exogenous nature of the COVID-19 shock. Our findings show that firms with ERM exhibit significantly higher market value and lower systematic risk during the pandemic compared with non-ERM firms. Moreover, these benefits are more pronounced among firms with more years of ERM experience, underscoring the importance of capability accumulation rather than symbolic adoption. The results help reconcile prior mixed results and provide evidence that ERM operates as a dynamic capability that shapes firm resilience in the face of severe external shocks.

title: Integrating an improved BIE technique with DenseNet for multiregional and multivariable thermal power generation prediction
affiliations: Shanghai Polytechnic University, Shanghai Polytechnic University, Shanghai Polytechnic University and Shanghai Polytechnic University

detail.title: Integrating an improved BIE technique with DenseNet for multiregional and multivariable thermal power generation prediction
detail.abstract: Multiregional thermal power generation provides grid stability, lowers dispatch costs, and mitigates renewable-induced volatility. To forecast this accurately, an improved binary image encoding technique (OBIE) is proposed, which converts the continuous independent variables into fixed-length native binary bit vectors and categorical variables into one-hot encodings. These are then arranged into an image for deep pattern extraction. Specifically, the method reorders variables by their correlation and maps pixels using a new arithmetic progression model that enhances continuous variable representation. Subsequently, the image is fed into a deep learning model (DenseNet-121), which effectively mines complex patterns. Results on three UCI datasets (Iris, Adult, and Diabetes) show that our method attains state-of-the-art performance, while variance analysis clarifies the critical contribution of the OBIE preprocessing step.  Moreover, our method attains a MAPE of 8.41% on thermal power generation forecasting across 27 provinces in China, using wind and hydropower generation as independent variables. This result outperforms both traditional machine learning models (BPNN, XGBoost, and LSTM) and existing image conversion baselines (BIE).

title: Remaining useful life prediction of bearings using an enhanced neural network with a novel activation function
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and K. N. Toosi University of Technology

detail.title: Remaining useful life prediction of bearings using an enhanced neural network with a novel activation function
detail.abstract: Rotating components are commonly used in several industries such as transportation, manufacturing and power plants. Bearings are considered as critical components in rotating machinery. Thus, the remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of bearings is regarded as an important process in bearing prognostics and health management (PHM). This study presents a new framework for predicting the RUL of bearings based on signal decomposition and a modified neural network that employs a novel Sine–Sigmoid activation function, referred to as Sinmoid. The proposed model consists of three main parts. Initially, the original vibration signal is segmented, and salient statistical metrics of the segmented data are calculated to construct a statistical feature dataset. Subsequently, the statistical metrics are decomposed using Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to reveal the underlying degradation behavior of the bearing. Finally, the neural network equipped with Sinmoid activation function is employed to predict the RUL of the bearing. The model was implemented on a rolling bearing dataset prepared from the PRONOSTIA platform, and the results revealed the superiority of the proposed model in comparison with other approaches.

title: A Term Structure Framework for Green Bond Spreads and Portfolio Strategies
affiliations: Finance Department, UTS Business School, , University of Technology Sydney - Business School, University of California Santa Barbara and University of New South Wales (UNSW) - School of Mathematics and Statistics, University of Technology Sydney (UTS) - UTS Business School

detail.title: A Term Structure Framework for Green Bond Spreads and Portfolio Strategies
detail.abstract:
The term structure of green bonds plays an important role in determining pricing practices and informing green bond portfolio design. We introduce a novel green bond yield spread measure, derived from the term structure of yields to maturity embedding curve-based information into bond valuation. We screen structural attribute associations of green municipal bond curve-based spreads using a machine learning technique "Association Rule Learning" and find that taxable green bonds with intermediate maturities and short durations are systematically linked to positive spreads. Screened green bond groups then inform the construction of tenor-and duration-based portfolios that deliver lower drawdowns and higher, more stable risk-adjusted returns relative to Treasury, particularly during periods of monetary tightening, while hybrid portfolios preserve most downside protection benefits. This superior performance is attributed to curve-level pricing and structural composition. The term structure framework develops profitable portfolio strategies to inform investors, issuers, and regulators in shaping transparent and efficient sustainable finance ecosystems.

title: Motherhood Penalty and Childcare Constraint: Global Evidence from a School Closure Shock on Labor Supply
affiliations: Center for Global Development, affiliation not provided to SSRN, World Bank and World Bank

detail.title: Motherhood Penalty and Childcare Constraint: Global Evidence from a School Closure Shock on Labor Supply
detail.abstract: This paper provides global evidence of a motherhood penalty and childcare constraint. Using national school closures during the COVID-19 pandemic-era as a quasi-natural experiment we isolate the effect of a large childcare shock on gender differences in labor supply and firm survival. We leverage novel high-frequency enterprise data collected via Facebook in 2020 and 2021 from a repeated cross-section of approximately 150,000 firms. We find that the closing of schools differentially impacted women, who were 3.5 percentage points more likely to close their business than men during the pandemic. This translates to women entrepreneurs having a 23% higher likelihood of closing their business than men as a result of a school closure policy. The effect is driven by women with children and is stronger in societies with traditional gender norms. Non-parent labor supply does not respond to school closure policies. Our paper reinforces the need for investing in formal childcare to support women’s economic empowerment.

title: Beyond Alpha - Why Financial Education and Behavioral Discipline Outperform Investment Selection in Long-Term Wealth Management

detail.title: Beyond Alpha - Why Financial Education and Behavioral Discipline Outperform Investment Selection in Long-Term Wealth Management
detail.abstract: The present wealth management system bases its client success evaluation on investment choice and return generation as its primary elements. The paper opposes this belief by combining research from the last forty years which shows that investor actions instead of investment returns determine how wealth grows over time. The behavior gap which costs average investors 1-2 percentage points each year exists according to DALBAR's Quantitative Analysis of Investor Behavior (1985-2024) and Morningstar's Mind the Gap studies and Lusardi and Mitchell's fundamental financial literacy studies. The S&P 500 outperformed average equity investors by 848 basis points during 2024 because of their incorrect market entry and exit strategies. The research investigates how different population groups including men and women and people from various age groups and with different income levels and racial backgrounds experience different levels of behavioral wealth destruction. The groups which face the highest risk of behavioral wealth destruction through their behaviors lack proper access to conventional advisory services. The following section demonstrates through randomized controlled trials and practitioner-based case studies that particular financial education programs result in measurable improvements of people's savings abilities and their credit scores and their complete financial wellness. The Education-First Advisory Framework consists of three fundamental components which are Knowledge, Discipline and Accountability. Financial advisors who change their practice model from alpha-focused to education-focused will achieve better client results because their new method produces stable business operations which keep clients coming back. The research presents its findings through recommendations which address both current practice and upcoming studies and governmental decisions.

title: No Place Like Home? The Cost of Mandated Local Investment in China’s Government Guided Funds
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: No Place Like Home? The Cost of Mandated Local Investment in China’s Government Guided Funds
detail.abstract: Government-guided funds (GGFs) in China manage over RMB 15 trillion as of 2025 and frequently impose a Local Investment Ratio (LIR)—a policy mandate requiring a minimum share of capital to be invested within the fund’s home region. Using a hand-collected dataset of 133 GGFs from 2009 to 2024, we examine how LIR stringency affects the IPO exit performance of GGF-backed portfolio firms. We identify a non-monotonic relationship: moderate LIR requirements (up to approximately 1.3× the baseline) are associated with a higher likelihood of successful IPO exits, but further tightening significantly reduces IPO probability. We explore the underlying mechanisms and find that excessively stringent LIRs constrain cross-regional syndication, lower syndicate quality, and deter elite co-investors—regardless of institutional type—while also increasing the incidence of investment style drift away from general partners’ (GPs’) core expertise. Importantly, GPs with patient-capital characteristics substantially attenuate these adverse effects, suggesting heterogeneity in managerial capacity to navigate policy-induced constraints. Our findings highlight how local investment mandates interact with governance and syndication dynamics to shape entrepreneurial firm outcomes.

title: The Verification Hill
affiliations: Cornell University

detail.title: The Verification Hill
detail.abstract:
Generative AI has made content creation nearly costless, but determining whether AI-generated output is reliable remains expensive and depends on scarce human expertise. We develop a theory of verification hierarchies grounded in a new economic primitive: the Verification Hill. Using standard sequential testing tools, we show that expected verification time peaks at intermediate beliefs (maximal uncertainty) and approaches zero as beliefs approach a stopping boundary. The peak arises because the prior determines both the starting position relative to boundaries and the probability weights on evidence paths; at maximal uncertainty, these combine to maximize expected time to resolution.

Three results follow. First, when verification capacity is scarce, optimal triage concentrates effort on tasks near the Hill peak-precisely the hardest cases. Second, hierarchical verification economizes on costly expert time through selective continuation: many tasks exit after coarse screening, and those that escalate arrive with a more favorable posterior, reducing expected senior time. Importantly, staging alone does not reduce total expected time if every task must continue (by the Markov property); the gains come from routing that stops many tasks early and reallocates initial evidence accumulation to cheaper labor. Third, combining this routing structure with Pareto-distributed stakes and convex expert supply yields the Pyramid Steepening Theorem: with task volume N , the junior-to-senior ratio scales as N B , where B = a8/(1 + a8) depends on the stakes tail (a) and supply convexity (8). The verification technology determines staffing levels; the economic primitives determine the response to growth. Extensions study incentives near the Hill peak, the plausibility paradox (improving AI can increase verification burden via subtler errors), and adverse selection under heterogeneous detectability.

title: How Does China Mitigate "Reverse Shocks" in Trade Networks? - Evidence from the "Shock Absorber" Mechanism of RCEP Tariff Reductions

detail.title: How Does China Mitigate "Reverse Shocks" in Trade Networks? - Evidence from the "Shock Absorber" Mechanism of RCEP Tariff Reductions

declarations.funderStatement: This paper is a phased achievement of the General Project of Fujian Natural Science Foundation (2025J011145).

detail.abstract: Grounded in complex network theory, this study conceptualizes RCEP tariff reductions as typical exogenous "tariff fluctuations." By constructing a Network-TVP-VAR model embedded with tensor decomposition, it dissects the dynamic transmission and reverse spillover mechanisms within the China–"Belt and Road" trade network. The findings indicate that: First, the trade effects induced by RCEP tariff fluctuations exhibit significant time-varying characteristics and network reverberation features, with institutional dividends showing increasing marginal returns over time. Second, the RCEP agreement functions as a critical "shock absorber." By reducing institutional friction costs, it effectively mitigates the "reverse shocks" of external risks, shortening the half-life of negative fluctuations by approximately 50%. Third, China has achieved a structural leap within the network, transforming from a "processing and assembly base" that passively absorbs fluctuations to a regional "stability anchor" capable of dampening reverse shocks. This study provides micro-empirical evidence for understanding tariff transmission mechanisms under complex networks and safeguarding industrial chain security.

title: The Enclave Penalty: Tribes, Caste, and Electricity Reliability in India
affiliations: Oklahoma State University - Stillwater

detail.title: The Enclave Penalty: Tribes, Caste, and Electricity Reliability in India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: India has achieved near-universal electrification, yet large inequalities persist in the reliability of the electricity supply. Combining high-resolution satellite-based measures of electricity reliability-defined as the share of nights with detectable illumination-with village-level census data, this paper shows that reliability remains systematically unequal across social groups. While Scheduled Caste villages largely track district-level reliability, Scheduled Tribe (ST) villages face a pronounced enclave penalty. Homogeneous ST enclaves (ST population ≥ 90%) exhibit 10.7 percentage points fewer illuminated nights than otherwise comparable villages within-district with low ST shares. We further identify a mobility trap: homogeneous ST enclaves are about 16.6 (16.0) percentage points more likely to remain energy poor in 2012 (2019) and 11.7 percentage points less likely to escape energy poverty between 2012 and 2019. These findings suggest that as access becomes universal, infrastructure exclusion increasingly operates through a less visible rationing of service quality in socially homogeneous tribal settlements.

title: How Does Data Visualization Affect Retail Investor Information Processing and Trading?
affiliations: University of Texas at El Paso - Department of Accounting & Information Systems and University of Colorado at Boulder

detail.title: How Does Data Visualization Affect Retail Investor Information Processing and Trading?
detail.abstract: Using three complementary research analyses centered on the Robinhood trading platform, which displays earnings visually, we provide convergent evidence that visualization facilitates retail investors' processing of and trading on earnings information. First, we document that Robinhood investors' trading around earnings announcements is more sensitive to visual earnings surprises than non-Robinhood retail and institutional investors. Second, a difference-indifferences analysis around Robinhood's 2017 introduction of visual earnings reveals increased trading sensitivity for high-Robinhood-ownership stocks. Third, a framed field experiment with retail investors confirms that visualization improves their ability to recall earnings surprise direction (i.e., their information processing). However, our archival analyses show that Robinhood investors trade asymmetrically. Net buying increases with the magnitude of negative visual earnings surprises but is not associated with the magnitude of positive surprises, a trading pattern that departs from a rational benchmark given the positive relationship between visual earnings surprises and future returns. Our findings demonstrate that visualization helps investors use earnings information to trade, but it does not correct the beliefs or preferences guiding how they use it.

title: Emotional Yields of Collectibles
affiliations: University of Cambridge - Judge Business School, University of Missouri, Columbia and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Emotional Yields of Collectibles
detail.abstract: We propose a novel method to estimate emotional yields of collectibles based on factor mimicking portfolios. Using up to 110 years of collectibles returns for 13 distinct asset classes, we apply machine learning techniques to address challenges from non-synchronous trading. We use these estimates to study how emotional yields affect equilibrium pricing. Emotional yield estimates for 24 of our 30 collectibles return series are positive, with an annualized mean (median) of 2.64% (2.53%). Despite various forms of underestimation, these results provide evidence that assets with positive emotional returns have lower equilibrium financial returns.

title: Competition between Asset Managers over Relative Performance Fees

detail.title: Competition between Asset Managers over Relative Performance Fees
detail.abstract: Two fund managers are paid by relative performance fees and compete for the maximum welfare from managerial compensations in the long run. The optimal response given the competitor's portfolio exploits the fund's investment opportunity and hedges against the risk in relative performance, and is a function of the endogenous competitiveness factor describing the comparison between the fund's investment opportunity and the competitor's return. It helps characterize the equilibrium by the roots and boundary values of cubic functions on closed and bounded intervals, which is simple for numerical implementations. In addition to the comparison between two investment opportunities, the equilibrium also takes into account of the optimal behavior of the competitor. It makes the equilibrium the middle case between the managers who are paid performance fees only based on the fund's own return history and those who are compared to an exogenous uncontrolled benchmark, as discussed in the previous literature.

title: Predictive Tail-Risk Regression for Heavy-Tailed Time Series
affiliations: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics, Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE), Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE), Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE) and

detail.title: Predictive Tail-Risk Regression for Heavy-Tailed Time Series
detail.abstract: This paper develops a robust predictive regression framework for estimating conditional expected shortfall (ES) in heavy-tailed time series. ES has become the regulatory standard for risk management under the Basel framework, yet its estimation and inference remain challenging due to non-elicitability, sensitivity to heavy tails, and serial dependence. We propose two complementary approaches to address these challenges. In the linear setting with heavy-tailed responses and predictors, we combine smoothed quantile regression with adaptive Huber regression in a two-step procedure, further robustified through covariate truncation. In the nonlinear setting, we introduce feedforward neural network (FNN)-based estimators for conditional quantile and ES functions, which adapt to low-dimensional structure and mitigate the curse of dimensionality while remaining computationally feasible. Our theoretical results provide non-asymptotic guarantees for both linear and nonlinear models, including deviation bounds, a Berry-Esseen-type theorem supporting inference, and oracle-type error bounds for FNN estimators. A key technical innovation is a coordinatewise coupling method that extends Bernstein-type inequalities to α-mixing processes and enables sharp distributional approximations. Simulation studies demonstrate the robustness and efficiency of our procedures compared with existing joint quantile-ES regressions. Empirical applications to Fama-French industry returns and U.S. macroeconomic indicators highlight the practical relevance of the methods, uncovering cross-industry heterogeneity in downside risk and revealing macroeconomic tail vulnerabilities.

title: Dynamic Hedging in ETFs and Income Generation through Protective Puts and Covered Calls
affiliations: Independent, Independent, Independent and Independent

detail.title: Dynamic Hedging in ETFs and Income Generation through Protective Puts and Covered Calls
detail.abstract: Most option-overlay research relies on theoretical constructs such as Black-Scholes pricing and fixed-interval hedging, offering limited guidance on real-world implementation in emerging markets. This study develops a market-executed, dynamic option-overlay framework that integrates protective puts and covered calls for two major Indian equity ETFs-NIFTY and BANKNIFTY. The overlay activates next-month at-the-money protective puts only after meaningful declines from a rolling reference level, while out-of-the-money weekly calls are sold during stable regimes to harvest time decay. Using actual traded option data and ETF prices from 2015-2025, the framework is evaluated across diverse volatility environments, including the COVID-19 crash. For the NIFTY ETF, the options overlay enhanced annualized returns marginally from 13.4% to 13.6%, while significantly reducing maximum drawdown from 33.67% to 15.58%. In addition, portfolio beta declined sharply from 0.487 to 0.226, indicating a substantial reduction in systematic market exposure due to the embedded hedging component. Applying the same framework to the structurally higher-volatility BANKNIFTY ETF yielded similarly robust risk-adjusted outcomes. While the baseline CAGR moderated slightly from 13.3% to 13.10%, maximum drawdown improved materially from 47.45% to 31.51%. Concurrently, beta declined from 0.486 to 0.187, reflecting a meaningful dampening of market sensitivity. Although returns decreased marginally in certain cases, the pronounced reductions in drawdown and beta highlight the effectiveness of the overlay in adding a hedged profile, materially improving downside protection while preserving long-term equity participation-even for indices with elevated volatility characteristics. Across both ETFs, the strategy outperformed the unhedged benchmark on more than 80% of trading days, maintained close benchmark tracking, and generated balanced contributions from both protective-put and covered-call modules. Overall, the findings demonstrate that conditional, rules-based option overlays can significantly enhance the risk-return efficiency of passive portfolios in India, offering a practical and implementable framework for long-term equity allocation.

title: Integration of Drone-Based Geospatial Data for First Responder Decision Support

detail.title: Integration of Drone-Based Geospatial Data for First Responder Decision Support
detail.abstract: The increasing complexity of emergency situations has intensified the need for accurate, timely, and reliable decision-support systems for first responders. This study investigates the integration of drone-based geospatial data with geographic information systems to enhance emergency response coordination and operational effectiveness. Using a mixed-methods approach involving spatial analysis, case-based evaluation, and comparative performance assessment, the study examines how unmanned aerial vehicles improve situational awareness, route optimization, and risk assessment. Findings indicate that integrated UAV-GIS platforms significantly reduce response times, enhance spatial accuracy, and support informed decision-making under uncertain conditions. Unexpected challenges related to network stability and data latency were also observed. The study concludes that drone-based geospatial integration represents a critical advancement in modern emergency management, offering practical benefits for disaster response, urban safety, and public health operations. However, sustainable implementation requires improved infrastructure, standardized frameworks, and continuous professional training.

title: Evaluating the Impact of GIS-Based Early Warning Systems on Rural Emergency Healthcare Access

detail.title: Evaluating the Impact of GIS-Based Early Warning Systems on Rural Emergency Healthcare Access
detail.abstract: Access to timely emergency healthcare remains a significant challenge for rural populations due to poor infrastructure, long distances to healthcare facilities, and limited availability of first responders (Adeparusi 2025; Jasni & Majid 2025). Geographic Information System (GIS)-based early warning systems (EWS) have emerged as a promising approach to improve emergency response by optimizing routing, predicting hazard zones, and enabling real-time decision-making for first responders (Adeparusi 2025a; Popescu & Bărbulescu 2025). This study evaluates the impact of GIS-based EWS on emergency healthcare access in rural communities by analyzing spatial data, emergency response records, and stakeholder feedback. Results indicate that GIS-based systems significantly reduce response times, improve coverage of underserved areas, and enhance operational coordination among emergency services (Adeparusi 2024; Kumar et al. 2025). However, infrastructural limitations, digital literacy gaps, and terrain constraints can limit the effectiveness of such systems in certain regions (Akinwale et al. 2025; Adeparusi & Ajenifuja 2024). The study concludes that GIS-based EWS are instrumental in improving rural emergency healthcare access when complemented with targeted training, robust infrastructure, and integrated operational protocols. Recommendations include investing in spatial data management, expanding digital connectivity, and enhancing coordination between local authorities and first responders (Adeparusi 2025a; Ajenifuja & Adeparusi 2024b).

title: Integrating the Conflict Tree into the 5E Model: An Intervention Study on Verbal Violence Prevention Among Clinical Nursing Students

detail.title: Integrating the Conflict Tree into the 5E Model: An Intervention Study on Verbal Violence Prevention Among Clinical Nursing Students
detail.abstract: 【Abstract】Purpose: To examine the application efficacy of a conflict-tree-based 5E teaching model in mitigating verbal violence incidents among clinical nursing students. Methods: A longitudinal comparative study was conducted with 78 first-year (2021 cohort) and 80 second-year (2022 cohort) nursing students from our affiliated hospital. The control group received conventional instruction, while the experimental group underwent the conflict-tree integrated 5E learning framework. Post-practicum assessments included Nursing Professional Identity Scale scores, ruminative intrusion related to verbal violence, incidence rate of such events, and clinical mentor satisfaction ratings.Results After practical training, the experimental group demonstrated significantly higher scores in nursing professional identity scale (107.33 ± 0.07 vs 99.39 ± 0.11), ruminative intrusion related to verbal violence (11.29 ± 0.33 vs 9.16 ± 0.67), purposeful rumination (14.68 ± 0.77 vs 12.59 ± 0.32), and clinical mentor satisfaction (10.08 ± 0.59 vs 7.67 ± 0.64), with statistically significant differences (P < 0.05 for all comparisons). Conclusion The conflict-tree integrated 5E teaching model demonstrates significant improvements in clinical nursing students' capacity to manage verbal violence incidents, reducing occurrence rates while enhancing professional identity through optimized cognitive processing of traumatic events. This evidence-based approach offers a novel educational framework for addressing workplace violence in clinical settings.

title: Charting AI Governance Future in the Arab Region: A Policy Roadmap

detail.title: Charting AI Governance Future in the Arab Region: A Policy Roadmap

detail.abstract: The Arab region’s capacity for Artificial Intelligence (AI) governance remains limited relative to the accelerating pace of global AI developments and associated challenges. This gap hinders the ability of many governments in the region to push their countries toward joining the ranks of those benefiting from the AI revolution—both in developing the public sector and supporting economic growth and social development. Currently, the region remains reactive as a “recipient” rather than a “creator” or an effective partner. This reality calls for a series of policy interventions at both local and regional levels to empower the AI ecosystem in the Arab region. What are the policy directions that Arab governments can adopt to build an AI governance framework that is strategic, responsible, and inclusive? This executive report provides a roadmap for establishing an AI governance infrastructure through a set of strategic policy recommendations across seven key pillars. These recommendations are based on regional research that included hundreds of leaders active in the AI domains, from the public and private sectors. This report highlights the key findings of a field study covering ten Arab countries to explore the realities and challenges of AI governance. The study was conducted by the Mohammed bin Rashid School of Government’s Future of Government Center, in collaboration with global AI pioneers. The results of this regional research outline a multi-dimensional policy roadmap that dives deep into the region’s current capabilities and the hurdles it faces in catching up with the AI revolution from a governance and policy perspective, presenting them in a practical framework for public sector leaders.
